Whether you’re a fan of traditional kebab or looking for something new and exciting, Fusion Kebab will not disappoint. Highly recommend — this place is a hidden gem!

Kebab Craft at Liberty Station is a great spot if you like customizing your meal. You can basically build your own plate by choosing the base, protein, sauces, and toppings, which makes it easy to tailor everything to your taste. I ordered a plate with two sides and went with beef, veggies, and fries. Everything was flavorful and filling, and the portions were generous. It’s a convenient and satisfying option when you’re walking around Liberty Station and want something hearty but still customizable. I’d definitely come back to try different combinations.

A pretty decent kebab place. Nice, fast service! You can customize a lot of items which is good since there is no many vegetarian savory places at the market! It was better tasting than what it looked. Not the best falafel pita I had but pretty good!

My sister and I came to Kebab Craft on a Saturday night at 7pm and I ordered the beef shawarma loaded fries with chipotle, tzatziki, and garlic sauce. The food was soooo yummy and refreshing especially with the tomato and onions!! Fries were very crispy and cheesy! Just wished they added more beef lol but very great portion size for it being $15. Customer service was great, the cashier was very nice and helpful on recommending and explaining the food items. Food didn’t take long to arrive (possibly because we came at a time when it wasn’t that crowded) But overall, everything was very delicious!! ☺️

I had the Chef's Cali wrap and it was fabulous!  The delightful young woman who took my order recommended the Chipotle sauce.  She nailed, it was perfectly paired.

If you go to Liberty Station, definitely give them a try!

Soooo good!!! Took our chances off the map after a day at Sea World. Amazing fresh food! Had the mezze platter and loaded fries, everything tasted super, and the Baklava… I would come back just for that.💜

Wow, talk about some amazing food and service.  This has to be one of the best Ethiopian restaurants I’ve been to in America.  It’s a hole in the wall for sure, but that adds to the charm.  The person waiting on us was so kind, so nice, so helpful.  You could see him literally running to the back to place orders and run food.

The table next to us was a little complicated.  He told them they weren’t setup for tea or coffee on a Monday night.  The diners insisted and he finally said, you know what, I can make it for you, but it will not be presented as normal, but I can make it in the back, to which the diners agreed.  He ran to the back and next thing you know, tea and coffee were brought to them….extraordinary.  As a former restaurant worker, I’d have not asked them to go through the effort, but this was above and beyond.

When I was leaving, they had some bread on the counter and I asked what it was and he described it and then gave us some to sample….it was amazing!

Anyway, we had the #1 special (it’s spicy but not super hot..for reference, I eat 2-3 Thai chilis raw with just about every meal, so YMMV) and the vegetarian combo.  It was all so so so very delicious.  I will definitely be back!

Awash has wonderful, flavorful food.  The best option is to go to the restaurant first and speak with the owner about what you should eat and how spicy things are before you try ordering online through DoorDash.  Ethiopian food can be variable depending on his it is prepared.  We visited for my birthday and followed the owner's recommendations based on our parameters.  We were not disappointed.  I enjoyed the ribs and other beef dishes.  They have Ethiopian coffee, beer, and Mexican Coke (cane sugar based) products.  The ambiance is nothing spectacular; the restaurant is the front half of a convenience store with an eclectic mix of goods worth browsing (Italian Panettone, butane grills, beer/wine, motor oil).  Definitely worth visiting for the food!

Delicious, soulful Ethiopian food in a humble and welcoming spot. We had the veggie and meat combo and everything was full of flavor. The Ethiopian coffee was the perfect finish. Great host and a great experience overall. Highly recommend.

For dinner we just stayed in and DoorDashed food. We started off ordering Beef Sambusas (Pastry shells stuffed with onions, jalapenos and Ethiopian herbs. For main course we ordered Awaze Tibs (Beef tenderloin or chikinia bits sauteed in onions and green peppers, cooked with Ethiopian butter), Yedoro Wot (chicken cooked with Ethiopian spicies, berbere sauce, onions, garlic and Ethiopian butter) and Kitfo (ground beef spiced with Awaze (Ethiopian hot sauce) and served with homemade cottage cheese, raw as well). It also came with some White Enjera and Teff Enjera to try with all the dishes. We really enjoyed the Awaze Tibs, that was great with the Enjera. The one we liked the least was Kitfo. The Yedoro Wot and Beef Sambusas were ok. Overall nice to try this cuisine but my stomach said that it is not for me.

Delicious food in the middle of an Ethiopian market. It’s kind of cluttered and messy. The service was OK. We waited a while even though they didn’t appear overly busy. The food arrived quickly after ordering.

Amazing service and absolutely delicious food! 10/10 — I highly recommend. Truly the best Nigerian food around! The owner was incredibly friendly, helpful, and had great conversation with us, which made the whole experience even better. We can’t wait to come back!

DO NOT EAT HERE

This restaurant is the worst place I've ever eaten. I saw cockroaches and rodents ALL throughout, and if that wasn't bad enough I got FOOD POISONING that lasted all weekend. Not to mention, there staff is incredibly rude and when we asked to speak to the manager the owner of the restaurant was extremely loud and disrespectful, in front of our whole family.

If I could this rat infested place NEGATIVE stars I would!! I reiterate...

DO NOT EAT HERE

I came here excited to try food from a highly rated place. Opened grimy doors and ended up in a gray empty space that was kind of scary with a white guy sitting in the middle. He was friendly but the space was not. I could not imagine having a meal there. It didn't smell like any delicious food or any food either. Super weird! I looked closely at the reviews and they are all placed by people with 1 or 2 reviews today so that's definitely sketch. I'm giving it 2 stars because well, what if it's a real restaurant with good food? I just know I won't be trying it after what I saw.

Let's start with the vibes. When I walked in, it was definitely a hole-in-the-wall. One review said it was "sketchy," and I kind of get it, it's not the most inviting space. It feels run down and not exactly like a place you'd want to dine in.

That said, I didn't want to be too quick to judge. California is expensive, and it's especially hard for small, ethnic restaurants to maintain a dine-in space while serving labor-intensive dishes. As someone who's Caribbean (Dominican), I get how much time and love it takes to make meals like this, and I respect that hustle.

I ordered the egusi, red stew with beef, jollof rice, and got fufu added on at pickup (shoutout to the staff for that, I didn't see it as an option during checkout, and they threw it in for me on the spot). The service was warm and genuine. My food was ready in about 30 minutes, and they were super sweet during pickup.

Now, the food. Flavor-wise, it was solid. The egusi was well-seasoned, though the color threw me off , I'm used to egusi being more yellow, but this one leaned red, so I'm guessing they might've mixed in red stew. The jollof rice was very seasoned, definitely a standout. The fufu was okay, but something about the texture or flavor was slightly off. Not bad, just not the best I've had.

The biggest disappointment was the red stew with beef. For almost $20, I got two tiny pieces of beef. That felt stingy, though not entirely surprising. I've seen this happen before at West African spots. Still, I expected a little more protein for the price.

Overall:
* Food is flavorful and portions (aside from the meat) are generous.
* The service is friendly and accommodating.
* The physical space needs some serious love, it could turn people away at first glance.

Would I go back? Probably not, just because I'd like to explore other spots that might offer more consistency. But I do think they're doing their best, and with some improvements to the space and portions, this place could really thrive.

Buka has never disappointed me. The food is always fresh, full of flavor, and made with care. If you're ever in City Heights, do yourself a favor and stop by. It's one of those places that truly feels special

Very nice food.
Old style, original Ethiopian environment.
Feels like home, best African restaurant in San Diego.

Say it with me
DEL-LISH-OUS

I have frequent this authentic Ethiopian Restaurant during the past few years of living in San Diego, and I still can't get enough!.  Food quality, presentation and of course the most important, TASTE!

The owners are truly blessings to the community. Upon entry, the restaurant has a museum like feel, highlighting great Ethiopians and art from the culture

I HIGHLY RECOMMEND  stopping by for a taste for any occasion!
Ask for the Honey wine!

So delicious! We had the Yedero Tibs and the veggie special which came with 7 types of veggies. We also got a sambussa as an appetizer which was super crispy. It was a great way to try a variety of flavors. We’re excited to come back again!

I was hesitant about writing a review bc I wanted to gate keep this restaurant for myself but this is a small, family owned business. This will be my go-to restaurant for Ethiopian cuisine in the SD area. The depth of flavor and spices along with the portion size and price is unbeatable. The service was a highlight and I saw that the waitress happily answered a lot of cultural questions for the other customers too.

I had a lovely experience dining here. The food was delicious, they accommodated my gf request, the service was amazing, and the atmosphere was adorable. The food was flavored and spiced perfectly. I will definitely be coming back!! The owners were so sweet and down to earth. You can tell how much love and care they put into their food. Parking in the area was easy. It was very reasonably priced as well :)

Delicioso!
Ordered the Tilapia, Coconut rice and plantains. My stomach is more than satisfied and the customer service was above and beyond. The fish skin was crispy and well seasoned.  I have to warn you that the coconut rice is highly addictive so please proceed with caution ⚠️

I walked into the store front which was very confusing because there are multiple restaurants that advertise food but it was only possible to order the African food on the kiosk. There is no one working in the store front so the kiosk is the only interface.  I was the only one there and I ordered two lunch specials. I assumed it would come out quick since I didn’t order very much and there was no one there, but I waited for over an hour to get the food.  Despite the wait, the food was very good and tasted homemade.

They gave me, what looks like Uncle Ben's yellow rice instead of Jollof. I'm so disappointed in this service from fellow Nigerians.  The goat meat is just covered in tomato sauce, not seasoned. I'm upset that the server tricked me. This was not a mistake. This was done purposely. If they couldn't fulfill the order, they should have cancelled it.

When i take the time to write a review is because the food or item either didn’t meet my expectations or as in this case it was beyond my expectations. Also there aren any pictures which can be helpful for future customers.

I was so scared to order and spend money when trying something new specially because i am very very picky but with this one i took the risk.

Red Stew (w Goat Meat): My favorite dish out of the 3. It was a tomato base, slightly spicy (a lot less spicy than buldak instant noodles). It might have some oil you can see on the top of the container just mix it up and you'll. be alright. This dish has so many Caribbean flavors might be the reason i loved it. Oh, Goat meat 100% cooked and very soft meat.

Egusi Soup: It taste so good i can’t describe what it taste like just know that it taste great and it has flavors. The egusi consistency is like scrambled egg, soft to me is excellent because i thought it was going to
be grainy and i hate that texture on my food.

Sauté chicken:  Taste goods. At the time of this review i haven’t eaten that much, main focus was on  the red stew.

Fufu: One ball of fufu got me full, i bought 6 of them thinking it wasn’t going to be enough 😂 but it is.

I wont be ordering again simply because the restaurant is very far away from me and ubereats fees are insane. But hey a least this time i have no regrets spending $90.00 for food.

I am very satisfied, thank you very much ! ☺️

I should have read the review before placing my order! DO NOT order food from here except you talk to them on Phone! I repeat DO NOT. I am a Nigerian and most of our restaurant service or turn around is poor but this restaurant is the worst when it comes to wait time, customer service and delivery. Unfortunately, I was not able to get my order but I have asked for my refund which I am yet to get!!!  Believe all the negative comments I beg you, they are true reflection of their service. If you want to eat tomorrow then order today because chances are that, there will be excuses as to why they have poor turn around time when you order. I have never written a review in the last 5yrs but for this restaurant and what they did to me I just have to.

Note to Owner: PLEASE, hire a food consultant to help position your service better than what you have. It SUCKS AND ANNOYING!!!!! 😡😡😡😡😡😡😡😡

name: Busy Bee Cafe
vicinity: Zoofari Party Area, Skyfari East, Zoo Pl, San Diego

reviews.text: The busy bee cafe is one of the most hot busy places in the San Diego zoo. All the beverages and the snacks have a huge demand the lines are very long collection and taking orders is quite efficient. I enjoyed the veg burger and the ice tea. Also for my granddaughters, loved the French fries. It's a very nice place with an ple shaded seating area to enjoy the food after you have taken it. Also, another services, the free water provided to the flood. Everybody whoever asked for it and they do it with a smile. I like the vibes in the cafe. Very, very happy to visit it. I think one of the best places to see happy footfalls will visit again

We ordered a simple family pizza and family corn dog meal. $150+. Watched several groups behind us getting their order. Started getting Suspicious. Asked about it, told it's coming. 30 min later, asked again. It's still coming. After an hour, we said we needed a full refund, we didn't come to the zoo to sit and wait for food. Manager was great! Full refund, instant fresh food and 3 ice creams. Good redemption, but still wasted an hour of expensive zoo time.

Liked the name of cafe which is situated inside the zoo and it aligns with zoo perfectly.
As name suggests, it’s always Busy ☺️.

Yes, good place to enjoy meal that can be enjoyed in the zoo. You get quite an option for veg meals or drinks while you need to energize taking the tour of the zoo.

The prices felt overpriced and seems its double the amount for a vegetarian meal.

This is one of the few restaurants at the San Diego Zoo with a vegan meal so it’s on the one I most often frequent when I visit the zoo. They have a decent vegan burger and their shoe strong French fries are so tasty.

There’s plenty of seating right outside the cafe and a confinement section too. Plus there are some ala cart items to pick up in the check out line like honey sticks, Powerade, and cupcakes.

The workers clearly have not been through customer service training. They could care less that they are even there or helping customers that are paying a lot of money for food that isn’t even worth that amount of money. When I picked up the food from the guy at the counter and said ‘thank you’ he basically shoved it toward me and moved to the next. My daughter got a refill on her drink but when my son tried, he was declined and told refills were only for water. I then tried and told the same thing. When I told the female worker she refilled my daughter’s drink and not my son’s she made some comment about ‘store policy.’ At least be consistent. Probably time for some customer service training and a complete staff overhaul.

10-11-2025
Happy Saturday!
I drove by this place at least 3x weekly  never knew it existed. My friend invited me to come dancing. I thought, “Why not? It’s only 6.3 mi from my house.” Glad I went, fun experience listening to Latin music and watching ppl dancing; I had to leave early so I didn’t get a chance to dance, next time lol

My friend and her friends ordered Papa Rellena ($6) and Empanadilla ($5); they enjoyed it. I, however, didn’t ordered any food but had Lulo drink ($6.45). My very first time trying it, refreshing!

Note:
-Regular hours, order food at the market counter.
-Dancing hours, start @ 9 pm. I believe the entrance fee is $5. In terms of food, it’s full service from Snack Menu.

Have fun dancing y’all!

I had a great dining experience at this South American restaurant today! The moment you step inside, you’re greeted by an exotic little grocery store selling authentic South American spices and grocery items, which sets a unique vibe. Turn left, and you discover a cozy restaurant with a bar and coffee station.

The menu features dishes from countries like Colombia, Puerto Rico, and Brazil. Every dish we ordered was bursting with flavor and made with incredibly fresh ingredients. The portions are generous, and the prices are very reasonable for the quality. My personal favorite dish is the avocado salad—the dressing is light and refreshing, and the avocado portion is impressively generous, making it a healthy and delicious choice.

Another standout was their signature corn tortilla, made from fresh corn that’s cooked, ground, and crafted with care. The texture and taste are worlds apart from typical cornmeal tortillas—truly a labor of love and a must-try. Every dish we had was a delightful surprise, showcasing the rich diversity of South American flavors.

This restaurant has been a local gem for over 40 years, and this new location lives up to its reputation. If you’re curious about South American cuisine or just love great food, I can’t recommend this place enough. It’s a fantastic spot to explore bold, authentic, and beautifully prepared dishes!

I will not be returning to this establishment. I ordered three entrée plates at $19.99 each based on the appealing menu descriptions and photos. We ordered takeout, and upon arriving home and opening my order, I was very disappointed. I ordered the Lomo Saltado, which was advertised as containing beef, tomatoes, onions, cilantro, fries, and rice, however, my order was missing the cilantro and there was 1 hidden tomato. Additionally, the dish was excessively salty. My son’s meal was also overly salted. Overall, the experience was disappointing, as the food did not match the quality or description presented.

I do enjoy coming here to get some good Latin eats.

I ordered the chicken Pastelitos and a Cuban sandwich. Both were very flavorful and delicious. I over-ordered. Lol. I couldn't eat the entire sandwich, I had to take it home. But was still delicious later.

My friend ordered the Arroz con Pollo with beans and a salad. He enjoyed it. But would have preferred not to have big chunks of chicken.

When we came in on April 5th, there were 2 women at the register. They were having a conversation which seemed more important than greeting customers.

Afterward, the young lady who was the order taker was not friendly at all. I felt like I needed to rush to give her my order. Not pleasant at all.

Once we sat down, our order came out fresh and hot. Again, delicious. The server was nice.

There was no wait and eat getting a seat. I suppose I'll be back. Knowing what not to expect is half the battle.

Come in for delicious eats. I also enjoy the bodega as you walk in.

I always put the most honest reviews not like some of these people that get discounts on the food.. Anyways, the rice just tasted different to me. Not that good, but it could be cuz. It's from some other place because I'm puerto. Rican, the bacalito was good, the Chicharron was not good.
But the service was very good. I personally will not go back because it was very expensive. And what I don't get is the pastel was black, didn't taste bad, but it was black. I asked them why they said because it was frozen for so long. Okay, that does not sound good to me. I used to get pastel from my mom and have it in the freezer for a long time. And it never turned black. So that broke the camel's back right there.I'll never go back.But if you want to just go try it go ahead But don't order too many things, because it's very expensive and you don't really know if it's fresh

Really good Jamaican food!! The curry chicken was delicious and the jerk chicken smokey, tangy, and had a little spice, they have lots of fun drinks and an authentic menu!  Definitely worth trying, over and over!!  Takeout is standard but they have a Jamaican decorated dining room with 6 or 7 tables

I am visiting from Maryland and wanted some good carribean food. When I tell you I picked a winner with Island Spice Jamaican Restaurants!. Beef Pattie was amazing and you can tell it's made fresh. The curry chicken  rice and peas. Perfectly made and seasoned.  I want to thank you for making such an amazing meal!

I smelled delicious food cooking as we walked up people getting their orders to go people seated waiting on food for dine in every table was full the young cashier guy was very sweet and welcoming ordered food was brought out to us it was delicious hot,fresh wonderful I will be coming back I purchased a large jersey meal great portion size I ate in but I left with a meal from my left overs because portion was very generous excellent food customer service

Island Spice shares the same parking lot as Alanberto at the corner of College Ave and University Ave, across the street from Taco Bell. You can’t miss the Jamaican colors.

We ordered a large plate of curry chicken ($17), large plate of oxtail ($22), and small side of jerk chicken ($12).

We ordered for take out and the second she handed over the boxes, I was shocked at how heavy 3 boxes were. When we got home, I was in awe  at the portions! So much food!

The entrees came with the protein choice, side of veggies and red bean rice. Everything was delicious and we had left overs. The chicken curry and oxtail were so tender it fell right off the bones. I used a plastic fork to eat and the meat had no problem. Great price, portion, taste and service.

Overall rating: 8.5/10

Ordered the oxtail small plate which was more than plentiful for one person. This is my first time trying Jamaican food so maybe I’m not the best critic. The meat itself was well seasoned and cooked very tender. My only reservation is that I found the taste to be a little too sweet. Knowing that scotch bonnet peppers are typically used in the traditional recipe, I expected it to be a little spicy, but it wasn’t in the slightest.

As someone who's lived in the M.E. for a long time, let me tell you, Abraj Mediterranean Restaurant is a true gem! Stepping inside, or even just tasting their food, transports me right back. This isn't just "close" to authentic; for me, it's the closest thing to true Middle Eastern flavor I've found outside the region. Every dish tastes like it's made with genuine passion and traditional recipes.

What really makes Abraj special is the owner. He's incredibly hands-on and genuinely one of the nicest people you'll meet. He's often on his own, handling everything, so yes, preparing your order might take a little extra time. But let me assure you, it is absolutely worth the wait. You can tell he takes immense pride in his work; the food is always prepared with meticulous care, cleanly, and beautifully presented.

Whenever I'm having cravings for Middle Eastern food, this is my absolute go-to. It's not just delicious; it's also really affordable, and you get a generous amount of food!

A perfect example of his kindness? My daughter absolutely adores his rice, and he consistently gives her extra, free of charge. It's these small, heartfelt gestures that truly set him apart.

I sincerely hope this wonderful business prospers and that its legacy continues for generations. It's places like Abraj, these fantastic small businesses, that truly make our community better. Do yourself a favor and try it!

Abraj was such a joy to discover and visit. They have the most authentic Iraqi food that I have ever had, and it is entirely thanks to the owners maintaining it themselves to keep the quality to highest standard possible. The food may take some time (15-20 minutes for main dishes, and appetizers get rolled out fast). The food is worth everything. The owners are extremely kind and sweet and take care of the customers very well and are extremely accommodating. They are dedicated to preserving the most authentic food experience, and this makes Abraj one of my top favourite Iraqi restaurants (and I have been to many across the countries outside of Iraq).

First and foremost, the golden dish that sets the tone for the entire meal: the complementary lentil soup, prepared in the authentic Iraqi style with a dash of paprika for added flavour and a slice of lemon ready to be squeezed and added into the soup. Truly, it is the best way to open the dinner table and satisfy the hungry stomach and get it ready while the heavier meal items arrive. Lentil soup to all arabs is something of a comfort food that speaks of so much love, warmth, and community. It is a symbol of home. This soup is no different, and elevates the experience in Abraj from just a regular meal to a full joyful experience.

The potato chop is my top appetizer recommendation. Aside from it being my favourite home-comfort food item, Abraj prepares it in the true authentic style with the perfect balance of flavour seasoning and texture. It is an Iraqi food item that is a must for everyone to try at least once. We also ordered Kubat Halab which is another Iraqi staple that is very difficult to find. The hummus is beautifully textured and seasoned. The Lajam blajeen is seasoned in a deliciously flavourful way. I recommend trying it with and without a squeeze of lemon. The lemon allows the seasoning to be elevated and shine in such a way that the experience of eating it with and without the lemon juice is like two separate dishes and is worth it, your tastebuds will thank you.

For main dish, I very highly recommend the kufta kabob!! This is the first time I have ever had kufta kabob exactly how it should be prepared in the Iraqi style, which is extremely difficult to replicate. There is something about the exact specific proportions of seasoning and meat quality that makes Iraqi kabob so special. Truly, everyone should have this food experience in their life.

Nothing is spicy unless you ask for it to be added, some dishes may have black pepper.

Again, I highly recommend you make your way to Abraj if you have the chance or want an authentic Iraqi food experience in a small quiet corner.

My new favorite Mediterranean place in San Diego, a bit out of the way but last night it was the only Mediterranean open later at night and so glad, definitely bookmarking this place. Prices are fair and the portions are generous. And that lentils soup … 👌🏼👌🏼😍

After a long search I think I have finally found the place with the best Greek chicken shawarma pita sandwich and rice that I’ve ever had! The food is seasoned, fresh, and made to order. The chicken was tender and flavorful, all the vegetables were crisp, and the rice was cooked to perfection. The portion sizes and the prices are both phenomenal. The owner seems like such a kind man. Very personable! This place is a jewel in San Diego. I’lll definitely be back!

I stopped in here after a long day of work cuz I was starving and didn't feel like cooking, and I'm so glad I did. They're 4.7 rating caught my eye - now I know why. The owner was so kind and welcoming. He mentioned that he and his wife run the restaurant together, and you can taste the love and home-cooked quality in every bite. He even brought me a complimentary soup while I waited for my order because he overheard me saying how hungry I was - such a thoughtful gesture that meant so much. The food was incredible the garlic sauce alone was worth writing home about and the whole experience felt warm genuine and personal - nothing like the impersonal chain restaurants were all used to. We need to support places like this - family-owned made with love local businesses that are serving amazing food and treating people like actual guests. I'll definitely be back and I'll be telling friends about it too.  Highly recommend

I tried the brown stew fish plate and it was incredible. The flavors were rich and comforting, the kind of meal that makes you want to finish every last bite even when you are already full. Truly a dish worth coming back for.

Anyone who has anything negative to say about this place is out of their minds! Came here for some lunch and got the oxtail jerk chicken combo. Holy SMOKES! It was so delicious. The portion was huge. Everything was flavorful. As someone who has visited the Caribbean, I can say this is the real deal. Oxtails were meaty, jerk chicken had a nice kick and the plantains were amazing. I can’t wait to come back.

I got the jerk chicken & oxtail combo. Very tasty & portion was generous. The jerk chicken had a little kick to it but perfect for my palate & the best jerk chicken I’ve ever had. My friends & I enjoyed everything we ordered.

This place is so good, it makes me want to go to Jamaica. Its hands down the best Jamaican food in San Diego and I’ve tried ALL of them. Nothing compares or comes close.
The staff doesnt care about excellent customer service or politeness so if you come here for that, go somewhere else. But I love that them, straight to the point attitude and they dont care about your “special requests” 🤣
If you dont like spicy food or you have food sensitivities, go eat at Applebees bro lol
I would give this place 10 stars!

Best jerk chicken I have ever had! The sides are meeeeh don’t really like them. But all the proteins here is FIIIIIRE!!!! And the prices aren’t terrible either! I hear once a week! The patties are pretty good too!

Usually the go to Jamaican spot when visiting SD, their food is pretty good, portion sizes are enough, and food tastes fresh. The atmosphere isn't too bad, as they do have limited dining seating  and very limited parking space, which is a struggle trying to find parking nearby, when there aren't any parking spaces on their parking lot. Service timing is fair. For some reason, it seems as though they run out of beef patties quickly. We sat outside of the restaurant on their patio.

I ordered the Oxtail plate, with rice and peas, cabbage and plantains. Not overly salty, flavorful and Oxtails had enough meat on them.

I decided to give this place a try, again, because we heard of the change in ownership.  Sadly, different owner, same lack of basic customer service. Staff seem to be burdened to acknowledge customers upon entering (the exception is the young man with a speech impediment who is the only pleasant person there). The lady there ignored some customers in favor of others and was extremely abrupt with her responses and unhelpful.  I thought that I must have offended her until I asked 2 different people to retrieve my order and they reported similar experiences.
Initially,  the food was good but subsequently went downhill. When the food started matching the service,  it's time to stop patronizing. The patties were consistently good. Sometimes the meal has plantains, sometimes not; fish is sometimes red snapper, sometimes not and is instead a barely edible, overcooked aberration that rivals chewing gum; fried chicken meal has sauce, sometimes not. Request for sauce or condiments are completely ignored( I would pay for them if necessary)and if the order is made incorrectly ( their mistake), they expect you to pay for it ( small vs large order).  The last time we were there, the food was not good. We have had better service buying tacos at the food truck outside the home depot.

Food is delicious!! It can take a while for some of the menu items, but it's definitely worth the wait. We had the brown stewed chicken which was just so tender and flavorful. The fried chicken was great a well. The beef patties are flaky and lightly spicy. You can't go wrong with any of the menu items. Definitely give this place a try.  I guarantee you'll be back.
Outstanding food.  This place is laid back with a calming atmosphere.  We enjoyed the curry goat and oxtails plates which was way more than expected.  Each plate was enough for 2 to done

Nice restaurant. Went there with 2 of my co workers I had the curry goat with rice &beans and plantain, they both got  chicken curry and beef oxtail respectively. My goat has waaaaaay too many bones in it but it's goat (maybe) but I loved the crunchy cabbage. Nice music I love Bob Marley he was playing slowly in the background.

The chicken is always moist and so delicious, they bake and grill the chicken with special seasoning and lemon. I order the half chicken ala carte with a Greek salad. The Gyro meat Is my 2nd favorite because it's never thin they serve so much Gyro meat I can never finish it. The Greek salad is always fresh and I always get extra feta cheese.

Food is ok. Nothing spectacular and they charge for any sauce 50 cents for tzatziki. Service was not friendly. Girl working seemed really unhappy and robotic. And kept taking phone orders while I was standing in front of her trying to place an order. $5 for a side of fries is also ridiculous.
Very good food and friendly service too!  The dining room is a little rough... Seems like most people we're doing takeout.
Excellent restaurant. I really enjoyed the food and our waitress.
The best gyro deal in La Mesa. My wife loves these gyros and she's a picky eater. Her favorite drink with the combo is the tall, glass Mexican Coke. The food is consistently the same great quality.

The best chicken and waffles I’ve ever had! First time I had these was over pandemic when we ordered for take out. It took over an hour but when we opened the box, I was surprised that the waffles were not soggy from all the steam. It retain its texture, the flavor was semi sweet and I didn’t need to use syrup. That’s how I like my waffles and to me, that’s a major bonus.

The chicken was juicy even though it’s white meat. The flavor in the breading was on point as far as spice levels.

Fast forward, post pandemic, we’ve revisited several times and this past weekend, it was just how I remembered it.

The location shares a space with the donut shop. Parking in that lot is tight, you would be lucky if you found one. It’s also not the best area.

There are a few tables inside to dine in. We ate it fresh and took 30 minutes for our order to come out. Recommend to call in your order.

Prices are reasonable, the combo #1 came with 2 tenders, waffle or fries and a side. The mac and cheese wasn’t super creamy. It was a perfect mix of cheddar and Parmesan.

Ali’s fries were also a nice treat. Similar to carne asada fries with all the toppings. We got chicken instead of shrimp. The spicy chicken sandwich was not spicy. They said next time, to let them know that we want it higher than Thai spice

I also got sambusas, which are similar to empanadas or samosas but different shape. Choice of filling, I got savory. This was not my favorite because of the dried texture. The chicken curry just needed dipping sauce.

Overall, we would come back here again and again.

Food is so good I had to come and leave a review through my job’s email! Awesome location with plenty of options. I got the Original Chicken Sandwich combo & it never disappoints. Definitely recommend getting it with their Ali’s Sauce. A must visit in City Heights. ✨

Incredible comfort food and great vibes! Ali’s Chicken and Waffles hit the spot! The chicken was crispy, juicy, and perfectly seasoned, while the waffles were soft, buttery, and just the right amount of sweet. The combo is seriously addictive. Staff were friendly and welcoming, and the portions were generous. Whether you’re grabbing brunch or a late-night bite, this place delivers on flavor and hospitality. Definitely coming back!

The best chicken sandwich in San Diego. The spicy is seriously good. We love their mac and cheese, and fries. First time trying a waffle and chicken here and I must say that was great too. Pro tip: order online via toast app, so that your food is ready upon arrival. Also,  It's so good that you might want to order more than 1 sandwich per person ;)

Simply the best.
Limited menu.
Just Chicken and dipping sauce.
Same ideal motip as Raisin Cane Chick Fil a
I love all sauce especially Coconut Sauce.
Chicken tender was juicy and crunchy spice cover.
Thai tea was good.

Amazing food! I went with my family. We have order Gyro sandwiches, Gyros plate, and gyros ball over fries.it was very delicious. We all love it. they always offer you extra white sauce. Nice service, friendly people.
You all must try this spot
100% recommending

Got gyro and hummus. The meat in gyro was tooooo salty. Took one bite and it was more than enough to realize that it’s impossible to eat. The hummus was too garlicky. The guy was kind enough and brought just grilled meat. The meat was still salty and greasy. Can’t understand how this place has high rating.

Highly recommended! The delicious Gyros we ever had with the white sauce. Huge portion, it was very tasty and they have been making homemade Dubai chocolate, which are also very yummy. we will definitely come back.

Such a gem in the neighborhood! Visited for the first time today and mad I’m just learning about it. The food portions were HUGE and it was absolutely delicious. The woman working was so so nice and we got our food super fast. I highly recommend this place.

Such a cute little cafe serving incredibly delicious gyros! I ordered lamb & beef gyro and spanakopita and it was extremely yummy! The portions were huge. I could tell the ingredients were fresh, my order came out very quickly and it was perfect for after a long walk on the beach.
The vibe is very organic to the area - a small cafe near the beach where you can quickly grab great food. I sat outside, as I preferred that vibe to their interior.

The service was great, my taste buds enjoyed every moment, I took a large part of my order home, as the portions were insane. I’ll be back for sure!

I ordered the curry chicken with rice and beans, veggies and plantains with a side of  mac and cheese.

The curry chicken was moist, flavorful and cooked to perfection. The rice and beans were soft and fluffy and seasoned very well. The plantains were okay only because  I've never had them before so I didn't really know what I was looking for as far as taste goes.

The mac and cheese was super cheesy but didn't have much flavor so that's the only negative.

Reasonable price for the amount of food and for 2025. Service was good as well.

All in all, I'll definitely be back to try the other items on the menu!

Okay first time going I could smell the flavor from the outside. The food did not disappoint with the delicious bold flavors and yummy spices with great portion sizes as well. One of the owners Kenny was so kind and helpful. I’ve since come back to try the food again and it’s still BUSSIN!. I’m bringing my mom next.. highly recommend!
If you want the vegan option you should call ahead it’s so popular:0 so far I tried the jerk & curry chicken. Now the goat ! So yummy omg.

Customer service/hospitality could definitely use some work. Guy taking orders & working the front was not the friendliest. Food was bland and seemed thrown together with store bought sauces & marinades. We had the oxtail and jerk chicken plates, & a beef patty. The seasoning on the jerk chicken tasted like some type of BBQ sauce. The food wasn't terrible but definitely not worth the $54 we spent for 2 people to eat. Due to the previous reviews we had high hopes for a banging Jamaican meal.  Maybe today was just an off day in their kitchen, but we'll never know because we won't be returning. 😢

I ordered a large curry goat meal. At first glance I was disappointed because I know what curry should look like and it wasn’t giving but I gave it a chance anyway. The best thing on the plate was the plantains. The food was unnecessarily spicy but had no flavor I found 2 pepper stems in my food (pic for proof). Needless to say I’m not going back to find out if anything else is good. It’s a 1/10 for me.

The worst Jamaican food ever I am Jamaican Native and this is such poor representation of how delicious and authentic REAL Jamaican food taste like ! 1st when we got stationed in San Diego I was pregnant with my  oldest son that was in 2019 I had the food the guy who worked there at the time name was Collin he was pretty nice ! The food wasn’t all that but I gave them my support! I didn’t go back untill now thinking it would be better   and who ever the guy is in the front with all the tattoos has no manners! I called to see if they were still open  and he had an attitude from the start ! Typical  ! But when I got there it got worse . He was nasty for nothing while I’m asking questions he’s there watching football on his phone I asked about the menu he says everything was available but then tells me that their out of stew chicken all while having a conversation on his phone out loud .Ok no problem . So on top of the horrible hospitality, the food comes out i ordered  fried chicken , oxtail, curry goat , jerk shrimp pasta , & 2 beef patty ! Kmt!

ALLL OF The food has no taste at all !!!! no seasoning so pepper (scotch bonnet) gravy is watery and salty and the veggies taste oily .  The curry goat was watered down. The patty was bready like it came out of the freezer  not crispy  or flaky at all The plantain dem taste like they been fried in old oil and the meat isn’t neatly cut up .  I am beyond disappointed not only because of the poor service but because of the robbery and foolishness this restaurant is serving and dishing out to customers. I understand that majority of  the customers are military and  not Jamaican or Caribbean familiarized but this is truly sad . The prices are ridiculous for the little portions and to add the food taste bad . When you try to support your own that won’t do anything but fail you in the end . As a born  Jamaican I can truly attest that this is not what Jamaican food is supposed to taste like!!! Yall need to do better and stop charging people for foolery. Get better chefs  and people who are genuinely working .  The worse !!!

Great place, great vibes. Could add more places with vegetarian savory options. I found a falafel place that wasn’t bad but the burger place was out of vegetarian patties two hours before closing.  Great seating options and great vibes outdoors and indoors!

This place is awesome! So much variety and everything we have tried has been awesome. Such a cool spot to hang out and grab a bite to eat. We will definitely to continue to come back every time we vacation this way.
Is a great place to come with family and friends that visit San Diego. Everyone can eat different foods at the market and wal along the place, play at the mini golf.
Various food vendors, seating in main hall have a beer or cocktail.  Small vendors sell excellent crafts, clothes jewelry, open air yard many museums with exquisite art

Went to Asado Gaucho, an Argentinian grilled meat spot.  Got the reverse seared pacana sandwich and the skirt steak burrito. Burrito was mushy and feels kind of greasy, wasn't a big fan. But the meat was good as I'm a big fan of skirt steak, maybe next time order the meat platter instead? The sandwich was pretty good, taste fresh with the herbs and meat was tender.

name: FLAVORS EXPRESS SDSU
vicinity: 5157 College Ave unit c, San Diego

reviews.text:
This place was delicious! Don't let the negative reviews fool you.  Yes, its not situated like a 5 star restaurant, but what you get in return is some quality, good tasting, and well portioned food. My daughter's shared a small platter and the wife and I a medium. It was more than enough food to share.  Service was also friendly which was a plus. The lady serving was a little quiet (which some people might mistaken as rude behavior), but you can tell she was friendly and wanted to make sure we had a pleasant experience.

Definitely recommend you give it a try

Everything is seasoned well, great balance of flavors. Chicken is still moist and the dark meat almost taste like steak the way he seasons it. The man behind the counter had good vibes that complemented the reggae. Next time i will get his name. 9/10 will eat again

Food is absolutely amazing! We got two Kubwa plates with saffron rice, sweet jerk chicken, spicy jerk chicken, curry chicken and one other that I forget but again just amazing! I cannot recommend this place enough. This was our first time but will not be our last.

Excellent food!  I don’t know anything about East Africa, but I had the saffron rice and eggplant and kidney beans with collard greens and LOVED the flavors.  Cumin in there and a lot of other flavors.  The guy who served it up was from Kenya!  Wish a place like this existed near my home

One of the best unexpected meals I've had in 2024. Excellent flavor and quality ingredients, you can tell the food is made with passion. Put simply, just really well prepared food with lots of different main and side options to create your own plate.

This was sooooo good! We come to La Jolla all the time and I don’t know why we didn’t eat at this restaurant sooner. We have walked by it a million times and finally tried it! The food was incredible- we had the chicken skewer platter and gyro fries. The chicken and meat were very good, the pilaf was delicious, salad, veggies, tzatziki and hummus too- all 10/10. Highly recommend this place, we also sat outside by the fire and it was super warm. Service was fast and the atmosphere was great, not too busy for Friday night. The prices are great for the portion of food you get.

My friend and I split the gyro platter (beef and lamb). Had a good amount of meat (crispy) with a good amount of fries and pita bread. Ask for a little less dressing on the salad if you prefer it not so wet.

We had three girls with us and they all got the kids menu with chicken nuggets and fries. Less than $10 each.

The happy hour wine for $7.00 was pretty impressive with the selection and their HH choices looked pretty good too.

The ladies behind the counter were very nice and helpful.

Went to Spiro's twice, once about a year ago and once today. The first time we went it was very good, had an inviting atmosphere and the food was tasty. Compared to today there are noticeable changes. The service was not as welcoming or helpful and the food was not nearly as good. I had the chicken kebab pita, which was drowned in sauce and had maybe 5 pieces of chicken. It was very underwhelming. However, the lamb and beef gyro was delicious and came with plenty of meat. I do appreciate how they have free water and a clean bathroom. I feel like today was an off day and Spiro's is hit or miss or the quality has declined over the past year. Overall, I would still recommend it for a Mediterranean lunch if you are in La Jolla, but generally there are better options nearby.
Nice location, quieter than the other restaurants in La Jolla as it tends to be crowded usually. The food is good and customer service is great.

We were walking around La Jolla and found this spot. The person serving was very kind and I don’t think I’ve ever had a gyro that had so much filling/meat! The Gyro fries were amazing too and the restaurant had calm vibes. Our food was served very fast too.

The service is above average—friendly, efficient, and on top of things. The bagel? Solid. The coffee? Hits the mark. Nothing groundbreaking here, but if you’re looking for a no-fuss spot to grab a quick bite and decent caffeine fix, this place does the trick. A dependable pit stop in a neighborhood full of options.

The staff are some of the kindest people in the business and I truly enjoy grabbing my coffee here. I love taking clients here and friends and family who are visiting in town. The Turkey 2 is a must and their vanilla lattes are incredible. I cannot be more of a fan.

Great spot for a quick coffee and breakfast! Service was great and fast, and the food and coffee was good. Not too busy on a Sunday morning, there was indoor and outdoor seating, everyone was pretty nice, good music and atmosphere

The traditional is a cold breakfast meal, and it looks simple yet delicious, and we liked it. The Turkey melt is a tasty warm breakfast, a little greasy with a good amount of Turkey and cheese. The Americano is average. I don’t recommend the matcha latte as it’s too sweet and barely matcha. Fresh fruit is always good, just overpriced.

This place is most suitable for a single party or small parties, as their standard table is for two people. Pets are welcome to dine with their owner at the outdoor seating.

It would be nice if the staff could clean the table sometime. A few tables were dirty, and we wiped down ourselves before seating. We didn’t see anyone clean the table throughout our meal.

I visited this cute little coffee shop in morning, during my visit to San Diego. I had some time in my hand, and had some work to finish. So I decided to sit in this cafe with a big cup of mocha, a muffin and a bagel with cream cheese. The morning breakfast in this place was fine. The coffee was good, the cake/ muffin was even better. The bagel was usual. The staff is friendly, and the place is quite popular. The cafe was extremely busy while I was sitting there. Everything is good, only the washroom is not inside the cafe. If you need to use it, ask the cafe staff and they will direct you there. The cafe wifi was enough good for me to work good. I highly recommend the place.

Outcast Grill is a local University City restaurants that’s been hanging around for years. It’s surprisingly good food for a local haunt, and they have a nice beer selection on tap too. I’ve been here at least 5 times over the past 6-7 years, but came recently with my brother and had a great time.

We ordered hummus and pita, a couple of Hazy IPAs, and some water and sat at the bar. The hummus and pita was honestly delicious. It was super fresh, and the bread was incredible fluffy and well-made. The hummus was creamy, flavorful, and the portion was on point.

I’ll need to come back sometime soon to review more menu items, but I’ve started taking this spot seriously. It’s really good.
The food is fresh and tasty and made with love. And the new menu has chicken enchiladas (green and red) which are amazing. Plus other new tasty items.  And they have great beers!

Very cute place with great atmosphere and vibe. Have been wanting to go here for a while now, nice location, kind of a small lot but also has street parking.
We got there around 6:45 pm on a Wednesday and they were steadily busy, the pizzas looked amazing on tables as we walked by! We ended up all going with fish.
Being a Wednesday, they had wine and pizza specials -we didn't even know! 😊 So check out their daily specials on food &/or drinks!!! We shared a J Lohr Cabernet, very smooth, not dry, hint of sweet but not overly.

Hubby- Fish & chips; nicely breaded, good firm fish (think it was cod), good flavored & tasty tarter sauce,  perfectly crispy fries.

Friend- Grilled Salmon Dinner with steamed veggies & basmati rice, veggies were a bit al dente however very fresh with a very good earthy flavor, rice was ok, regretfully her fish was a bit fishy/not as fresh, over cooked, and under seasoned...needing a side cup of the vinaigrette that came with the salad. She ate about 1/2 of it and then couldn't continue.

Me- Mahi Mahi burger & greek salad; salad was super fresh & loaded with feta, olives, cucumber slices, cherry tomatoes, & red onions -it comes with a slightly sweeter thick vinaigrette which wasn't bad; the buns were toasted, loaded with pickles, sliced tomatoes, red onions, lettuce, a generous spread of tarter sauce, & a good sized portion of Mahi Mahi...the Mahi was a bit over cooked however seasoned well and still very tasty.

Staff were nice, did frequent check ins and were quick with any requests (the extra dressing).
Most incredible local spot. Their shakshuka was so delicious and amazing. Their salads are incredible. Awesome draft beer selection. And a great place for family and friends.

The service was great the food, not so much.
Everything seemed to be frozen except for the Calzone. The Cajun pasta sauce was pretty thin and flavorless as was the chicken in the dish. The burger patties seemed frozen and everything was slipping out of the bun. I'd say the highlight of the meal was the French fries and the Calzone. We probably won't go back. Prizing is pretty high for the quality of food.

name: Itacho Sushi - All You Can Eat

reviews.text: This was my first time trying this restaurant, and we're definitely planning to come back again. The sushi was really good, and the service was both friendly and attentive. The atmosphere was also very pleasant. They offer good quality sushi with plenty of variety, along with a selection of drinks to enjoy.

I’ve come here multiple times and have always had a great experience. The host Janna was quick to get me seated and explained the the ayce options when we got there. Food was great for an ayce restaurant. I highly recommend the hibachi and lo mein! The owner was also very friendly and inviting. If you’re looking for affordable ayce sushi definitely come here!

Abdul and todays crew Dec.12 were out of this world awesome. Very accommodating and funny as hell as they all were rolling with the punches. My compliments to the awesome delicious food and the atmosphere is excellent.  Sorry guys we were pretty loud but that was only because it was my birthday and you guys made it even better.  Definately will stop by again.
ALL YOU CAN EAT AND BOYYYY DID WE 4 ATE....LOL

We came into Itacho Sushi at 7:30pm on a Monday night. No wait for a table for 4. Ample seating all spaced out, and staff were super friendly, welcoming, and helpful.

We opted for the AYCE platinum menu. Definitely recommend trying different single sashimi or nigiri and picking your favorites. The dishes tasted fresh and flavorful! Some of my favorites were the unagi, ikura, squid, seared salmon, king mushroom salad, and escolar.

Also helpful to remember your order each passing round (user error on our end). We certainly felt like we ate our money's worth with the variety. The hand rolls are generous, so I would opt for just nigiri or sashimi and salad next time.

Parking is ample in the lot, unlike other parts of Convoy. Our server was also really patient and attentive. The vibe inside is relaxed - there's a large dual TV that was playing football and a sushi mukbang.

For 4 people each ordering AYCE platinum menu, we paid 55$ per person including tip.

This had to be one of the worse Japanese restaurants I've been to. I already expected the quality to not be great since it was an AYCE place but man! There's a few different tiers to choose from, and they make you choose it before being seated.

The rolls presentation looked nice but the flavors itself were lacking. The sushi rice didn't have the distinct taste. It was rather dry, flavorless, and smelled as if it wasn't washed well or too old. That made the whole experience unpleasant, whether it was a roll or sushi. As long as it had rice, it didn't make me want a second bite. It was more like having to force myself to finish everything, if not everything was a la carte price, which still wouldn't be worth the cost. Sushi were plentiful with rice and fish fell right off the block as it was picked up.

I'm not even sure how to properly describe the appetizers. The fried calamari were cold, dry, and hard. Not pleasing to the eye, either. The mango salmon was more like, cut the salmon as you please in little snippets and throw it on the plate with some sauce, and drop it off at the table.

The only good thing about this place was timing. Everything came out FAST! That's it. Just rethinking about the whole experience makes me upset. It was an absolute waste of money!!

As a Nigerian, I pride myself in how much spicy food I can actually eat, and many spicy chicken sandwich places I’ve been too have been pretty disappointing. This place hit the spot!!! I ordered the lift-off spice level for the sandwich and tender combo, and it was probably one of my best bites since I arrived in the US. My entire mouth lit up with delicious heat, and it took me back to the days when I would eat a really nice bowl of pepper soup. If you like heat/spicy food, this is the place to go to. The strawberry hibiscus slushy tasted like “zobo” and paired really well with the sandwich. The staff was also friendly and nice. 100% would recommend!

I really enjoyed my visit to Houston TX Hot Chicken! The Sandwich & Tender combo is unbeatable, packed with flavor, great portion size, and cooked to perfection. The food is spicy in the best way, and the seasoning is spot on.

What stood out just as much as the food was the friendly and super fast service. The staff made the experience even better with their positive attitude and efficiency. Definitely a place I’ll be coming back to. highly recommended for anyone who loves quality hot chicken and great vibes!

Driest chicken we've ever tasted. The place was clean, in a great location, but we won't be back. There was a line to order off one tablet. We asked if they could just take our order and the two young men just looked at each other and spoke among them without acknowledging us. One of them slowly walked over to the counter with a frustrated look and took our order. The fries were okay and so was the sauce, but the chicken was the worst. The place needs customer service training, and quality control of their food. We were in a hurry and did not have time to talk to someone.
First time at the Houston Hot Chicken and boy we loved it. The chiken is tender is very good both with a salad and the chicken sandwhich. Prices are very affordable, defenetly a place to stop by.

I was in town for the Esri User Conference last week. Tuesday night, I needed dinner, so I wandered up the street and found myself at Houston TX Hot Chicken.

It wasn't very busy at the time, so I stepped up to the counter and ordered a 15-piece nuggets with fries. I selected buffalo on the heat scale along with ranch and house dipping sauces.

I sat outside and waited. After maybe 10 minutes or so, my order arrived.

The chicken and fries were both pretty good.  Next time, I might keep it to 10 nuggets, and I'd order two ranches instead of the house sauce. The house sauce was sweet, and I didn't care for it. The ranch, however, was pretty tasty.

Also, it was pretty crowded when I left. I guess I timed it just right.

Bottom line: I would definitely eat there again.

name: Kababayan Bakery
vicinity: 8423 Paradise Valley Rd # B, Spring Valley

reviews.text:
Customer service sucks here if you don’t speak Tagalog.  The ladies are so rude and speak the language with their mean faces. The food is delicious but the attitude man - I watched a Hispanic guy with his daughter treated like trash he was asking what type of foods were being served and they ladies looked at him with such disgust.  I’m have Filipino and I’m just appalled at how they treated this guy but he wasn’t the first I’ve seen it multiple times and in almost afraid when I get in line and ask me if I’m ready LOL.

It’s so sad to see because their food is delicious.

1st time trying them out, the staff was very helpful. We got 1 box meal with noodles and beef for $10 and 25 lumpias for $17 plus 2 cheese ball breads $1ea.= est. $30dlls for 2 ppl. IM NOT big on cheese at all but these cheese ball breads are my new favorite, YOU HAVE TO TRY THEM.

This is my second time around, great selection of hot & ready take out Filipino dishes. Had the chicken adobo and pork steak with pancit this time. Came out to $13.xx along with some comp sour soup. Everything with delicious. They had variety of bakery options as well. Store is connected to the Snoice drink shop

Their loompyas have gone downhill.  I had been buying loompya from them for the past 4 years until now. Never again.  This is the 2nd time recently buying the loompya and they extra garlicky taste to them now and not from fresh garlic. It tastes like they use the cheap Garlic powder.  It must be a new cook or owners. I don’t know but now their loompya are worst.

Definitely was craving some authentic Filipino food, so we stopped in to a spot that always has a parking lot full of cars.  Well upon arrival there is a sign that says 3 people only inside, remember to social distance. The food was displayed in the hot pans and the woman behind the counter greeted us with a smile..I joked with her because I was lookong for Pork Adobo, so I told her to bring me her dinner she cooked last night. She just laughed 😅. We ordered Chicken Adobo, Sisig, Lumpia, and Pandosol. The building smelled sooooooo good. There was bread on the shelves, she gave us fresh baked pandosol from the back. I even got the Quickmelt cheese. 🙌
The food TASTES AMAZING!! Now I know why the parking lot is always packed.  The adobo OMG!!! DELICIOUS I normally prefer pork but that  chicken was really good the gravy was not oily or had that vinegar taste as some do. The LUMPIA was light but very meaty. The SISIG was good, Fresh and the pork was tender. Check them out if you want some authentic food.

The food is amazing and fresh and the people who work here are just the nicest and friendliest people you've ever met. This is where you should go eat again and again. Even my picky kids love it, and the people here are so sweet to them.

The food is delicious and very good quality, prepared with love and reasonably priced. We usually go in for their specials of buy one get one free or on sale for $4.99. They have never disappointed us!
Great spot for a quick, quality meal. Staff was so kind. Price was extremely reasonable for the amount of food. Check out their specials Monday- Thursday too!

This has got to be the best Mediterranean I’ve had in some time. The food was both plentiful and flavorful and made with great care and attention to detail and presentation.
The staff was amazingly friendly and we lacked nothing in attention and smiles.
The chef even brought out complimentary tacos after my wife expressed disappointment that they were temporarily out of the tritip they use for their tacos.
I will write more later but had to get this out.

We will be back!

I had been wanting to try their food for a while because of all the good reviews.
I got a falafel wrap, chicken tikka plate, and Greek salad. They were all very good and worth the price.
I might not get the falafel again, just cuz falafel does usually turn out a bit dry. It was good but I, probably, try it once at every place I go to that sells it and then not likely order it again. 😅
But the chicken was juicy. Salad was flavorful. 🤤
My hubby is pretty critical of food and he said he wants to get food from there again and to have others try it.
So you've got return customers here.
I also want to say the service was very good. He let me know how long it would take for my food to be ready and he even separated the hot items from the cold item. I really appreciate the thoughtfulness.

This is a solid restaurant no doubt. Didn’t have any steaks but I have the impression that steaks here are great. The halibut was ok, the Chilean sea bass was great. Service is very professional. Highly recommend this place for a pleasant lunch or dinner.

By way of our anniversary, my wife and I spent the weekend in SD's Gaslamp District. We love ordering multiple items and sharing. I love the idea of, "family style" Lou & Mickey's offer. Our food was tasty but the "wow factor" was not present. My least favorite item on the menu was the spinach. I don't normally add seasoning to my meals at restaurants but the spinach was well deserving of a pinch of salt. We chose to eat outside but was met by an overpowering stench (I'll assume it was the ocean). The overall experience and atmosphere was great! I can't wait to try other menu items.

First time eating a 90 day dry aged steak. Honestly couldn't tell it apart from 40 day. If they had a 30-, 60-, 90-day aged tasting, it would be welcomed, to discover the nuisances, *hint*hint*. Was it tender? Absolutely. Was is flavorful? Definitely. I enjoyed the goat cheese appetizer but I had to request lightly toasted bread and honey which elevated the experience. The baked potato was another solid win. Would revisit in a heartbeat if ever back in town.

Five stars for sure for waiter Robert! Extremely, knowledgeable, and perfectly attentive without being bothersome. A very warm and relaxing atmosphere with a great location in the gas lamp District. Be sure to order the rolls. If you like oysters, don’t hesitate ordering them! I would drive age steak, that we shared, was very good… But I must admit that I’m parcel to a thicker cut, grilled perfectly by my husband. I have to mention our fabulous dessert!

My first time eating here and it did not disappoint! My ribeye was perfectly cooked and so tender. The balsamic mushrooms were my favorite side. The potatoes and asparagus were also good. The bread was definitely worth getting.   The real winner was the ponzu scallops!!! Oh myyyy!!!

Went out of my way to try this place but is was closed for lunch at 345 even though google hours said they were open. Call first.

In response to your response:

Wow, thats pretty harsh for all the google reviews about how friendly the place is. I understand the law and how important lunch is. I just want to make sure my fellow customers understand that its possible you could be closed due to unadvertised hours.  I have only encountered a few businesses  in america that shut their doors when they want and yes i always have the option of not returning. I will be back as I would love to meet you and understand why so nasty when I only spoke the truth. This is Regina's husband James.

As a man from the south, being out in California makes it hard to find things that remind me of home.

This was a great reminder of home and the pudding my grandmother would make at family gatherings.

Customer service was amazing, the owner is super friendly and welcoming to his buisness. He had samples out that helped me make a decision on what I wanted.

My only critique is that the website does not have all the flavors that he had in store. Granted I dont mind since it was a nice surprise to see stuff I definitely will try my next visit.

The gentleman was super kind and helpful!
The place is very open and clean but the pudding....oh my gosh.
It's life-changing I didn't know that I was missing this from my life. A texture similar to a dense mousse or like a whipped pudding. Airy, pleasantly fragrant, and the perfect amount of sweetness.
Absolutely the best pudding I've ever had in my life.

I admire this business for preserving old family recipes and offering multiple flavor options for their customers, but unfortunately we were not impressed by the taste nor the presentation. The chocolate banana pudding was bland, lacked any type of banana flavor, and had the consistency of mousse rather than pudding. We also tried the regular banana pudding which was a bit better, but still seemed on par with store bought pudding.

I don’t usually take my time and do reviews. But this place is a must try. Saying the desserts are good doesn't even come close—these are next-level delicious. If you're nearby, do yourself a favor and give them a try. You can’t go wrong with any dessert here.

My parents in law tried Korean food for the first time! We ordered spicy dawji galbi jjim, soy drumsticks, bulgogi, corn cheese, rice and of course banchan. The food was amazing, they loved it and I loved it too! We even had some leftovers. The place was nice, the servers were awesome. It was great dinner for us.
OMG one of a FEW late night spots in San Diego - is chill nothing over the top but friendly, respectful service. Highly recommend! Oh and if you have a FOODIE KID they'll love it here!

This was our second time at this place. I don’t like to give negative reviews on google but I am this time. Food was okay, it’s was better last than now. Service was bad. Only the girl Mikha was good. She was the best, other guy’s service wasn’t good, he doesn’t know how to serve. We were 5 people and 1 kid(18months) they charged service fee.
I asked the guy to give my baby a high chair that high chair was dirty and seems like it was just painted because it was sticky. I took a picture of it.
Hope they will get a new server like Mikha.
I wanna give 5 star reviews far Mikha’s service, because of their 18% service charged for 5
People I won’t be able to give you.

This place is exactly what we were wanting after a long day with the craving of warm Korean food late at night. Packing lot is a bit small but there's street parking.

When you are seated you order off the screen at the table. Select everything you want then send in the order. You can use it to also call a waiter over or Ali for the bill. It's perfect for people with anxiety of ordering.

The food came out fairly fast and man it was all pipping hot. Everything was what we were drooling and dreaming for.

Kimchi pancake was huge and so filling. The Gyoza Mandu were so tasty I would've gotten 2 orders; delicious and salty dipping sauce.

My ramen was very hot and flavorful. A bit more veggies than I expected and the beef was a bit tough. Still yummy I'm going to try spam next

The soondubu was boiling and ready for the egg to be cracked in. It was devoured.

Ambiance is so laid back there are booths lining the walls and tables in the middle too.

We can't wait to come here with our friends!!

I was craving some Korean food late in the evening and found a place open until 1:30am, so I dragged my friend to try it out with me. When we arrived, the waitress barely acknowledged us, leaving us to stand awkwardly at the door until she finally waved us to a table at the back. The restaurant wasn’t crowded, so we were surprised by the waitress's short and upset demeanor. It took a few minutes for her to bring us menus and water. After we ordered, we decided to draw on the blackboards covering the walls around our seat.

We ordered dduboki, sweet chili drumsticks, pork katsu, and a regular lychee soju cocktail. When everything arrived, we were pleased with the large portions. However, we noticed we received a large cocktail instead of a regular one. Despite trying to get the waitress's attention multiple times, we were ignored, so we ended up keeping the large drink.

Thoughts on the food:
- **Dduboki:** The classic dduboki is hard to mess up. Despite the $15 price point suggesting something special, it tasted good, though not exceptional for SoCal. 7.5/10
- **Sweet chili drumsticks:** One of my favorite dishes at Korean restaurants is their fried chicken. These were fantastic with perfectly crispy skin and a sweet yet spicy sauce. 9.2/10
- **Pork Katsu:** This dish leaned towards the drier side. The flavor was good, but the pork was too thin compared to the crust. 5/10
- **Lychee soju cocktail:** A tasty cocktail that made the night more fun. The large size was meant for sharing, but I enjoyed it alone. 8/10

I had an exceptional dining experience at Bombay Coast. The food was outstanding, especially the Shrimp Patia — perfectly balanced, rich in flavor, and prepared with incredible authenticity. Every bite was a reminder of how good coastal Indian cuisine can truly be.

A special mention goes to Mr. Zubin, the warm and gracious host and chef. His hospitality made the experience even better. He took the time to check on us, share the story behind the dish, and made us feel genuinely welcomed.

Highly recommend Bombay Coast for anyone looking for amazing food and heartfelt service. I’ll definitely be returning!

I absolutely loved our dinner here!

Chef Zubin and his team do not disappoint, this is our second time here and there will be a third, fourth and you get the idea.

Thank you for making our time memorable, the food brought back memories from our time in Mumbai and that meant everything.

We ordered:

Shrimp Patia
Eggplant Chaat
Vada Pav
Keema Saali Pav
Pav Bhaji

In our previous visit we had:

Shrimp Patia
Keema Saali Pav
Ginger Chicken
Chilli Garlic Cauliflower

Everything was great!

Being from Bombay, I recommend. So delicious. The kheema pav is a must. Also enjoyed their malai chicken, shrimp patia and seekh kebab. The employees are very sweet too. Not the typical boring menu you will find at other restaurants. The food tastes like a home cooked meal that you will find in India when there is an occasion. Will definitely come back for the kheema pav alone.

Loved the keema pav, the mixed kabab combo and the Rasmalai. Not many places specialize in Parsi and western Indian cuisine (Bombay /Mumbai specific cuisine belonging to Parsi, konkan and East Indians). Unique gem situated in a nondescript neighborhood mall in Clairemont. Zubin, the owner is a charming person, his affable personality and pleasant smile made us feel at home.
People should try the Parsi cuisine items from the menu, they will definitely not be disappointed.

I really enjoyed the food. We ordered a 3 entry combo and special lamb. The portions are large so we automatically get our lunch for the next day. Highly recommend the lamb and chicken. The lamb is soft and the yellow curry chicken has a great coconut flavor. I was here a few years ago, and they refreshed my impression of bombay coast as they did better than the bombay coast at UCSD (now closed). It's great that the food quality is still high after many years.

Fish & chips were fine. The clam chowder in the bread bowl was good. What was exceptionally disappointing was the salad. I didn't have high expectations, but for $20, I expected more than a portion the size of a side salad. Didn't come with dressing, had wilted lettuce, and the entire bottom of container was just cabbage.

We were on a walk with our pup in Seaport Village and we’re looking for a casual, dog friendly spot to grab a bite. Marion’s patio was dog friendly and had a good view of the bay so we decided to give it a try.

The staff was super nice and welcoming, and we appreciated the friendly service.

We ordered the grilled salmon taco, grilled mahi mahi taco, and a side of fries. The tacos were just okay—not bad, but nothing special either. The fries had a tasty seasoning and were our favorite part of what we ordered.

Although the food we tried was average,  the combo of the views, dog-friendly patio and friendly service made it a good experience.

Excellent fish and chips. Love the crab cakes! The family size order was enormous. We definitely could have shared one order of fish and chips instead of the family platter. The cucumber mint water is a very unusual flavor but I think I like it.

Andrea is amazing.  Her welcoming smile and overall hospitality is refreshing. As is the food and the service.  I had the traditional fish and chips.  The Pollock fish is light and flaky. Topped with their home made tartar sauce and seasoned french fries,  a true belly satisfier. Be sure to try the home recipe lemonades. Delicious!

We came to San Diego this week after moving away more than 22 yeara ago. These are by far the best fish tacos we have had. The owner was very friendly and engaging. Definitely going to come back again.
Each dish is better than the last. This is the food joint for people who work at food joints. Great decor and will definitely be seeing me again soon. Be on the lookout for their pop up events!

Never expected to be blown away by EVERY DISH we ordered. At 1st we were very reluctant that we would find something we would like because we aren't into all the gamey meats they had.... BUT my goodness, everything was perfect!!!  Or "fireeee" as my picky husband said!

The Baja Fresh Oyster appetizer was delicious! The flavoring was bright and fresh, it had all the flavor profiles to tantalize my taste buds, I could've eaten 2 doz!!! The Patatas Bravas scallops appetizer was also a hit as it was cooked to perfection. The sauce paired so well with it, my plate was wiped clean. Make sure to also get the tacos de lengua!!! The meat was tender but not too rich, and the salsa complimented the well seasoned meat even my 1 year old son was saying, "Mmmm!!!"

Hubby had the Our burger which was cooked perfectly. Every bite left u craving for more... n that says a lot when youre just eating a burger.

Also, the bread pudding was delectable!!!!

This place is a 10/10 and far exceeded all of our expectations!!! Make this place a must try if you're around the area!! Service was great too! Soo happy to have celebrated my son's 1st birthday here!!!!!

We hosted a company happy hour for a conference event in the upstairs private party space. The rooms were interesting, food and drinks excellent, and service impeccable. Evening was a success. Highly recommend!

If you want to have the best cocktails in all of San Diego, go here.

I had a cocktail with gin, chili, and katsuobishi. Incredible depth of flavor. Smoked sea salt garnish. Photograph below.

I had a tequila reposado with honey, and espresso, their take on an espresso martini. I forget the other elements of the drink but it was delicious.

I finished with a cocktail called Fat Boy Summer. By this time, I was feeling good and can’t recall the ingredients. But, again. Delicious.

The atmosphere  is swanky, moody and intimate. Talented and professional bartenders.

I spent $62 for 3 cocktails- worth every penny.

I’ll definitely be back.

Absolutely fabulous experience. The tacos were bursting with flavor and the meat was so tender it melted in your mouth. The venison sliders were juicy and thick. Every bite was perfect. Washed it all down with two shanties. I took the bread pudding to go and it did not disappoint.

name: Eddie V's Prime Seafood
vicinity: 789 W Harbor Dr Suite 158, San Diego

reviews.text: This was hands down the best experience in San Diego. The Sea Bass was 5 stars, seafood tower was 4 stars, and the dessert was 5 stars. Servers Alan and Eddy were the best host - 5 stars plus a bonus star for going the extra mile to makes sure our experience was top tier!! 🫶

The food was wonderful and the staff was incredibly friendly. I started with appetizers while enjoying the live jazz band. I especially appreciated that the staff allowed me to linger and continue listening to the music after I was finished eating; I never felt rushed or pressured to leave.
