We had the goat platter with rice n peas and plantain, smoke turkey egusi soup and goat peanut soup with 2 fufu to share. The drinks are pricey and smaller, but everything else was to be expected cost wise. The food was piping hot and absolutely delicious!!!!! We chose to sit down and even though it's a takeout spot the cashier was very welcoming and continued to check on us and even brought out our containers as they were cooked, restaurant style. Genuinely some of the most tender goat I've ever had 🥹 and the best egusi I've tasted too. We made it in the day before their last day of takeout orders, and the food is so good I would cater it just for the 2 of us 🤣 man. Ps, idk why all the complaints on portion size! It was big enough for us both to eat at the restaurant and go home and still have 2nds 🥳

I came across this restaurant when looking for authentic Caribbean and African cuisine and this restaurant delivered! I ordered their jerk chicken and oxtails and my husband ordered the curry chicken. The proportions are great and we had food for two days! The spice on the jerk chicken was phenomenal and it has been a while since I had jerk chicken with that spice! Definitely a restaurant to try and fall in love with! Staff is friendly, service was fast, and the restaurant was clean and welcoming. I loved the music they had playing and the decor is beautiful. I will be coming back to try their African dishes!

Food quality lacking I ordered the Jollif Rice with sides. Mixed veggies looked like they came out of a can, the chicken tasted old and dry, the rice and plantains were good but when I asked for if they sold a side of Egusi they said no. But when I asked for a side of plantain they told me they told me they don’t sell it as a a side!!!! (After he went back and asked the chef) Sounds like lazy chefs.

Absolutely delicious. I've had Ethiopian food but long ago. I remember it was good but not nearly as good as this. The server was very helpful, gave us suggestions for tibs and the veggie platter. Not only was the food delicious and healthy but the prices were amazing value.

The coffee was very good and the smoothies were the best I've had in a year. Honestly if you walk by you're doing yourself a disservice. Don't be afraid to ask for help from the service!

ugh to find good Ethiopian food in Baltimore, but thanks to Addis Ethiopian Restaurant, we finally got to enjoy authentic Ethiopian dishes in B’more. I loved the food—amazing service too! I’ll definitely be coming back often.

Ethiopian food was on my bucket list. Never had it before and the thought of using my hands instead of utensils was interesting. Food is served on a large tray with various veggie dips and meats surrounded by a tortilla type roll that when opened you tear off a piece and use it to grab the spread or meat. I have to say that the taste and flavor was unique and delicious. So tasty and definitely so fresh.
Service was professional and very helpful. I had their fruit juices doevificslly strawberry juice like a frosty consistency.
The only concern is location. Not being a native Marylander traversing through a tough area was interesting. The owners have been in business for 3 years. I highly recommend this place if you can get over driving in the heart of Baltimore. Fir me it was well w I ryh it. If your looking for unique flavors this is the place l ace.
On a scale of 1 to 5 with 5 being excellent zi give Addis Ethiopian Restayrant a 100.
It's that good.
Chef Woo Can
Find ne at Amazon books n s under the same nane.
YouTube: Chef Woo Can

Ordered the veggie combination and everything was great. The injera was spongy and tangy.  Each stew had the right texture and was extremely tasty. Our host was very friendly and welcoming.

No need to travel to DC; there is great Ethiopian food here in Baltimore.

Just got a takeout, and I am super happy with my meal. The food is fresh, super healthy, and delicious.
The people who run the place are very kind and generous. Definitely found my fav Ethiopian place in Baltimore.

Life is good as I write this review and thoroughly enjoy my suya lamb fried rice. However I can’t deny that for a $7 side of jollof rice I was expecting a large serving than I received and maybe a little more lamb meat (or maybe I’m just a hungry college student) but this is barely stretchable 😭

It’s also my first time ordering from Disbe so maybe I’m making a rookie mistake and this is just their typical size? Someone lmk

Ordered from DoorDash
The shrimp rice noodle bowl with extra shrimp was absolutely amazing. The flavors savory, sweet, spicy. Would have enjoyed this even better if it were warm… I wish there was a dine in restaurant. (Hence)

I also not sure about some of the reviews. I feel like the amount of food I received was well worth it! I am so very full right now lol. Also you can’t take in account the dasher time this has nothing to do with the restaurant.

Pleased that I took a chance on this restaurant I did some research and really respect what the owner has accomplished. Look forward to trying the shiitake mushrooms next! 10/10

I absolutely loved my order of jollof rice, mushrooms, and quinoa! The jollof was amazing, and I forgot to take a photo. Jide was incredibly thoughtful and made sure everything was perfect for my vegan preferences. Thank you so much! I’ll definitely be ordering again!

We ordered thru Ubereats. The restaurant called to let us know an item wasn't available and gave us a suggestion on a replacement. The food was awesome and they threw in something extra. We will definitely be ordering again.

I was starving at 2:30AM & wanted something good to eat. Of course its late and options are very slim then I stumbled across this Gem on DoorDash. Man the food was soooo freakin good and fresh that it blew my mind. I dont play when it comes to food, I know good food and got dam was this food delicious. The Jollof was so flavorful and fresh, the shrimp were seasoned to perfection, the noodles were fresh and full of flavor, my plantains were so fresh they literally taste like they just got finished getting cooked in my own kitchen. Don’t hesitate to order its a 10/10. Its so good im ordering it again today.

Turkey wings, chicken, and Pork chops with gravy were tasty and flavorful.

Sides were a bit disappointing. Macaroni was absolutely disgusting and had a strange flavor.

All in all I would eat here  again, but will try different sides.

Where do I start….. let’s start with the bbq chicken. It was horrible it taste like dish soap… Mac cheese taste like Mac with no cheese…. Fried chicken was about to fly out my tray with all them feathers on it.

This Carry out spot has food almost buffet style. You pick and choose what you want. Basically a protein and two sides. I got the wings, mac & cheese, and sweet potatoes. The wings were cold, but they were seasoned very well. The mac & cheese was a little watery and had no flavor. And the sweet potatoes/candy yams still had the skin on them and wasn’t even Sweet. This location is Carry out only there is no place inside to eat. As soon as you walk in there is the window for you to order and that’s all. Inside does look distressed. Probably could use some remodeling on the inside and out.
Don’t know if I was there on a bad day or not but the food was bland and nasty

Today, had smothered  pork chops with rice , gravy , collard greens, sweet cornbread with a grape soda. It was
$11.25. Yes, go to Yammi and get you
a delicious  soul food meal. My plate was good and the gravy was homemade and delicious. And, the other food look so desireable - prepared well. I recommend yammi's.Go and support them!!!

I came in during lunch time and the young lady was very courteous. I got a veggie platter with 9 options and a few veggie sambusa, everything was amazing. I have dined in and gotten carry out and I would definitely recommend this restaurant. The flavors were so good to me and the injera was soft and perfect.
First time the food was really good. Got the vegetable plate. And the Ethiopian beer was good too.
The vegetarian platter is top tier! So good!!! Plus they do have Ethiopian beer and honey wine. We will return!

Such succulent flavors for one who misses great Ethiopian Food (yeah, I’m calling out NYC for their overpriced Ethiopian). The Awaze Lamb Tibs were perfectly spicy and not gamey at all. The Shiro (chickpeas) were also wonderfully spiced and paired perfectly with the injera! The lentils and gomen were top notch! Service was fantastic! Everyone was so friendly and attentive!

This place is a gem, and absolutely worth a visit!

By far,  one of the MOST DELICIOUS food I have ever had in my life. Oh my!  We found this place about 3 weeks ago and we have been back at least two times a week since. The atmosphere is groovy, very hip and chic evenings during the weekend. Very quiet and calm during weekday afternoons and evenings! It’s a bit small but if they could ever get live Ethiopian music in this place…oh man, I’d move across the street just to be closer and spend the rest of my life at this place. The staff is very friendly and overall incredible!!
The best food in Baltimore! We're visiting from New Jersey and we're going to miss this place 😭 food was so good we had to come back the next time and try some more

Being from the deep south (AL), it's hard finding real soul food. The DMV is a total bust when it it comes to true soul food. Came to Baltimore (yes, I know it's not the DMV) and found this spot, and the reviews did not disappoint. I got the turkey wings w cabbage and fries . My partner got wings w sweet potatoes and mac. Everything was delicious. Although it was a tad bit too salty. Just a little. And the mac wasn't my kind of mac, everything was still so flavorful. It's inside the food court area. You can't see it from outside.

The service is what you'd expect because everything is made to order. Took about 15-20 mins, but we didn't care because it's not fast food. Blackfamilyy owned and operated. Very nice people. Clean. And they had a 90s playlist going. I can't wait to go back. The prices were what you would expect for the area. It reminded me so much of what I had in Alabama. Delicious home cooking. The only thing I wish they had was cornbread!

Staying at Inner Harbor and was looking for a black owned restaurant to support and came across this place (it's inside the mall).  We arrived @ 2pm and they were already out of collards and turkey wings. Not sure if they were sold out or just didn't have any for the day. We ordered the blackened catfish, shrimp, mac n cheese, yams, rice, and green beans.  I thought the green beans were a little too salty but other than than we found EVERYTHING to be very flavorful and would go back again.

I’ve been searching high and low for good fried fish in Baltimore ever since my favorite neighborhood spot closed, and Soul Kuisine came highly recommended. Located on the first floor of Harborplace, it offers a convenient yet slightly tricky location for parking, though it’s manageable. I was excited to try their food after reading that they serve actual catfish—a rarity these days when many places substitute other fish. While they have tables for dine-in, I opted for takeout.

The fried catfish was the highlight of my order. After making a stop on the way home, I tried it straight from the box. It was a bit soggy by then and rated about a 6.5 or 7/10. However, a quick two minutes in the air fryer brought it back to life, transforming it into a solid 9/10. This tells me that if eaten fresh at the restaurant, it’s probably closer to a perfect 10. The flavor was authentic, and the fish had that classic crispy coating that makes fried catfish so satisfying.

The fries were seasoned frozen fries—not bad, but not the star of the show either, which is fine since I was there for the fish. Overall, Soul Kuisine has earned its spot as my go-to for fried catfish in Baltimore. If you’re a fan of fresh, well-seasoned fish, I highly recommend giving them a try—just eat it there for the best experience!

To the nice young lady and the nice young man here you all are amazing!!!!! I had the mac and cheese bowl with chicken on top and it was sooooooo good!!! I also got lemonade which was delicious!!!! I am thoroughly happy with my experience here and will definitely be returning!!!! Keep doing what you do guys and may God bless you always!!!! See you soon!!!!😍😍😍❤️❤️❤️

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

I visited from the UK and had the chicken platter with sides and a smoothie, and it was absolutely delicious! The chicken was well-seasoned and cooked perfectly, the sides were fresh and flavourful, and the smoothie was the perfect refreshing touch. The service was warm and welcoming, and they made me feel right at home even though I was so far away. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip—highly recommend!

Food was delivered right on time and on point. Food so inviting and delicious. Packaging really sophisticated and presentable. Food uniquely different from the regular party food. The sauce spicy and tasty. My family absolutely loved the food.
I ordered two boxes of Guinea fowl with sides for my family. I must say we did not regret it at all. Really tasty with the right amount of spice! We thoroughly enjoyed it! We will be ordering again!

Afro Grill makes the best grilled guinea fowl, roasted yam and plantain in the DMV area. Customer service is top notch and the food tasted so delicious. I will recommend Afro Grill anytime. The grilled spicy guinea fowl with sides of roasted yam and plantain did not disappoint. Tasted so delicious. Keep up the good work. I'll definitely be back soon for continuous order 👍

I recently tried the grilled chicken from Afro Grill House, and it was absolutely delicious! The chicken was perfectly seasoned, tender, and juicy. The flavors were bold and well-balanced, making every bite satisfying. Definitely a must-try for anyone craving tasty, flavorful grilled chicken! I will try the rest of their menu soon.

I was very happy to find out that there's a new Senegalese restaurant in Baltimore and AJ's is great! We had the Thiebou Dienn (Jollof Rice & Fish) and the Dibi Lamb dishes which were delicious and plentiful! I highly recommend their Senegalese food! (Please note, there are no tables to eat at inside. It is best to carryout or have the food delivered from this location).

I was very surprised by how delicious the Dibi Lamb was! The flavors were amazing! I was looking for Dibi Chicken and the Baobab drink (Bouye). The only other places I could get Senegalese food was in Silver Spring or driving way across Baltimore. This location was close and their food was WAY better....OMG! The red onion sauce was spicy 🥵 🔥 I loved it! There is something about that Mustard sauce. Walahi you can eat a sneaker with that sauce! 🤣🤤

The Dibi Lamb portion was excellent 👌🏽!🔥🔥

The owner was very professional and kind and helpful. I found a new place for my Baobob fruit drink addiction!!

Go!!!🚗 They are legit. Mashallah. I'm very happy I went here this evening. Now I have a new place! They sell Nigerian and local American food also.

Man I dont usually leave reviews but this ish was AMAZING !!!! Ordered a fish dinner from here last night and I couldve fed my whole family off it. Large portion. Also customer service was A+++ . Thank you
The food is delicious, as always. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Also, I haven't tried drinks like theirs anywhere else, it is amazing! Recommend, 10/10.

I am so happy that heaven has come down in the form of this restaurant. Very nice people. I had their Cheh-boo Jen, and it was amazing!

I recommend everyone come on out and enjoy their food. They deserve the recognition!

Do not order the Ogbono soup. MAC was god awful. He was not willing to offer any accommodation

Edit: Aquira spends $25-$35 everytime that I come here and I’ve been about 10 times in the past 3 months. Aquira wasn’t expecting a “discount.” Aquira was expecting some compassion and understanding. I wasn’t nasty to you sir. I don’t see you as competition because I’m not your competitor I would like everyone to win. You’ve lost a regular customer. My biggest thing as a business owner is for a customer to be satisfied and for a customer to return. Any who I pray your business continues to be blessed. Just lost a a faithful customer in me. Take care

This business is a scam, the food is the worst food I have ever tasted. The owner doesn't take calls and the phone kept going to voicemail, so I had to wait almost 30 minutes plus to pick up my order. He finally opened the door and my order was incomplete because he said he didn't have the fried rice and plantains that I ordered and said he would notify DoorDash to refund me.
Guys read the reviews about this place, they are accurate reviews. This business needs to be shut down to the general public. These guys are wasting people's time and energy. Very dirty and unhygienic place. Again, read the reviews and stay away from this business. I will follow this up with the authority and ensure this business is closed.

I ordered a meat pie, Mac and cheese, a beef patty, and oxtail via Uber Eats. I actually ordered it at 11:30 PM and they close at midnight. The owner stayed open an extra 30-40 minutes just to get my driver the food (the drivers kept canceling). He was really easy to contact and communicate with, and I really appreciate that.

The order was missing the mac and cheese, but I was able to get refunded for that. The meat pie wasn’t very good; pretty dry. The beef patty was pretty good — the crust was slightly dry but the filling was flavorful and generous. The oxtail though was truly excellent. I only meant to eat a couple and save the rest for later — I devoured every last bit lol. They were tender and delicious.

Where do I begin, besides don’t waste your money. I ordered the peanut butter stew with okra. The peanut butter stew taste very burnt with an OVERWHELMING AMOUNT OF PEANUT BUTTER. And the okra was very bland. The total cost was 41.56 NEVER AGAIN DOOR DASH THANK YOU FOR MY REFUND.

I am a DD delivery driver. This place is not professional and nasty as hell.The place is really a house with a large kitchen. Just walk in the side door and you're in the Kitchen. Another note, the guy you talk to on the phone also is the cook and delivery driver as well. I've tried picking up here twice and was told by a large handicapped gentleman sitting in a recliner in a living room told me that the cook would be back. He was out making deliveries.
Needless to say I would never eat from here just from what I heard and saw there.

I wish I could give ten stars, this place is amazing. The wings and homemade vegan ranch were out of this world; the Philly cheese fake and pumpkin muffin were also incredible. I also had the chamomile pineapple Iced tea, which was amazing. They also have an amazing selection of organic teas. The waiter was super friendly and knowledgeable. I will definitely come back here next time I'm in Baltimore.

This was my first time visiting this restaurant, and it definitely won’t be my last! The food was amazing, and the drinks and smoothie were delicious 😋. We ordered the buffalo wings, guacamole with chips, a sandwich (can’t remember the name), the peanut butter berries smoothie, and the Phat Beet juice. Let me tell you we were not disappointed!

Each item had its own flavor, and you could taste the freshness in every bite. The prices were affordable and reasonable, the staff was friendly and professional, and the chef was clearly on point with his cooking. I don’t live in the area, but every time I’m in town, I’ll be making sure to stop here for a good Liquid Earth meal!

10/10 STRONGLY RECOMMEND.

I was in Baltimore and wanted to support a vegan establishment, so I decided to try Liquid Earth based on the great reviews and proximity to my hotel. Although it's on a busier street, the surrounding neighborhood has tree lined streets (some cobbled) with historic rowhouses. I enjoyed my walk exploring the area.

It was a hot day, and I arrived hungry! I started with a cup of the gazpacho. It arrived with a wheel of lime to squeeze on top and some crisp baguette toasts.  The gazpacho was so flavorful,  cooling, and refreshing. I could feel my vitality being restored as I finished it off.

For the main course, I ordered the Sacred Salad and asked to add a scoop of the tofu salad. This was a power move! The salad was a feast for the eyes as well as the palate- a work of art! The tofu salad featured pleasingly firm chunks of tofu in a creamy base and it was perfect for scooping up with all the fresh veggies and greens. I finished things off with one of the 2oz juice shots, 'the uninflamed,' made with ginger, pineapple, and turmeric. Delicious!

If you're in the Baltimore area, and even if you're not vegan, check out Liquid Earth. The atmosphere is welcoming and homey, service is great, the playlist is on point, and the food here is something special!

A friend and I came here for the first time today. I was so excited to have a vegan lunch but can’t tell you how disappointed I was with what I ordered.

Food is supposed to delight the senses. Please see the photo. Nothing about this makes me want to eat it. On top of that, I’m not sure that your kitchen understands what a burrito is. The onions and peppers in a mash of black beans? No sauce? A toasted tortilla? Not a burrito.

I sent it back as inedible and had the pleasure of paying for the experience. No not ok.

I won’t be back.

The food here is top tier — fresh, flavorful, and thoughtfully prepared every time. It’s hands down one of my favorite spots to enjoy delicious vegan and vegetarian meals. Highly recommend if you’re looking for plant-based dishes that actually hit the spot! ❤️

name: Lebanese Taverna
vicinity: The Charm'tastic Mile, 719 S President St, Baltimore

reviews.text: We had such a great experience here that we came back a second time during our visit in Baltimore. The humus was exceptional as was the falafel, kebabs, and stuffed grape leaves. The puffed bread and tzatziki brought it all together.  The service was exceptional and attentive and the setting was fun. We had so much food that we took home leftovers and ate them cold the next day. How could they even be better cold the next day?!? But they were 💕

Enjoyed our visit today to Lebanese Taverna! Yummy salads. Hummus and bread is EXCELLENT...The white Sangria with chopped peaches was dddeeeeeeeelicous! Bread pudding was not great, but everything else made up for it. Wonderful service and fun, hip location by the Harbor.

The stuff is amazing and the food is great. Mehdi was very polite and helpful to make sure we understood the menus and the food we were ordering. We recommend this Mediterranean/ Middle Eastern restaurant to anyone who want quality food and time spent in Baltimore.

Lebanese Taverna offers a wonderful dining experience with some standout dishes. The fresh, warm pita bread was absolutely fantastic, and the appetizers set the tone nicely, especially the cheese rolls, falafel, and kafta rolls, all flavorful and satisfying. The tabbouleh was bright and refreshing, and with just a squeeze of lemon and a touch of salt, it became even more delicious.

A couple of items fell short: the eggplant fateh didn’t quite meet expectations, and the chicken kabob (taouq) lacked the depth of flavor we were hoping for. That said, the overall experience was still very good, and the highlights, particularly the pita and appetizers, made it worthwhile. This is a spot we’d happily return to for its vibrant flavors and welcoming atmosphere.

The best middle eastern food my husband and I had. So fresh and burst of different tastes! We absolutely loved it and service is top notch! If you are in harbor east in Baltimore it should be a must stop!

We stopped by and were lucky enough to be the first customers of the day.

The falafel was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft inside, the hummus was smooth and rich, and the shawarma meat had that perfect Mediterranean spice that makes you want more. The pickles, pita, and sides all came together beautifully every bite felt refreshing and satisfying.

Highly recommend – 10/10

I ordered from Zaatar on Uber Eats. I got chicken kabobs, grape leaves, and baklava. The pita was completely covered in mold and made me sick to my stomach. I couldn’t eat the rest of my food. I’m not one to typically give poor reviews but this was honestly so awful.

I really wanted to like this place after reading the reviews. The hummus was great.  The beef shawarma was more like me a beef burrito in form and taste. The falafel balls were crispy on the outside but still raw on the very inside. I think the oil may be too hot. Here's the tell though..... Clean your bathrooms. It says so much about your restaurant that they're filthy. Overall mid-grade food but I would give it a second shot.

Very wholesome experience. The hospitality by owner was very warm and welcoming. The food was delicious without burning a hole in the pocket. We had ordered Chicken sheesh kebab platter along with Turkish coffee( must have) and mint lemonade.

Woah guys. Just woah. One of the best meals I’ve ever had at a restaurant. Rather go here than eat filet, crabs lobster. My mom and I went and got the hummus with beef shwarma on top with Pita. The fried cheese appetizer.  And the mixed kebab with chicken, beef, and Kifta. 10/10. The food was absolutely amazing. The server was very kind, attentive, and we did not have to wait for anything. Really nice place with Christmas decoration and beautiful Arabic music. SOOO GOOD HIGHLY RECOMMEND. Do yourself a favor and try them!

Absolutely amazing food and service!
Piazza 27 is my new favorite pizza spot! The food is always fresh and full of flavor — especially the chicken tenders, baked ziti, and Alfredo pasta. The pizza crust is perfect every time, their pizza cheese is super delicious, and the staff are super friendly and quick with orders. You can really tell they put love into what they do. Definitely recommend stopping by if you want great food and good vibes!
Highly recommend Piazza27 for anyone who loves great Italian comfort food! 🍕🍝👏

We asked for Chicken Masala and ended up getting chicken Alfredo !?? Got a quesadilla & I’ve never in my life bit into a quesadilla and tasted absolutely nothing before.. this is a first. The food is flavorless, nasty and thrown together like it’s someone’s first time cooking… I don’t see how this place is still open, everything I ordered I could’ve made at home.

When my friend and I ordered garlic knots, we were ready to be in and out within 5 minutes. We had arrived close to closing and were looking for a quick bite. When 20 minutes had gone by, we were a bit upset. We were the only ones there so what was taking so long?? Turns out it was well worth the wait. BEST garlic knots I’ve ever freaking had. The reason it took so long was because these must be handmade (at least it tasted like it) and not some frozen garlic knots that were microwaved. Warm, doughy, and garlicky - everything you could wish for.

If I come again, I’ll definitely be sure to order another set of knots!!

This is place is so bad it’s not even funny I went the first time for garlic bread like I saw on previous reviews freshly baked and when I got my order I received an old piece of a sub roll with butter and garlic powder put together with no effort the bread was hard not even soft I couldn’t even eat it smh. Another time at work the guests would sometimes order pizza from there and to my surprise it was good but when I go and order my pizza comes out burnt and the skinny tall guy behind the counter that seems very inexperienced and slow tries to tell me “do you mind extra crispy?” Smh thank god I looked at it because it looked burnt black edges not crispy this restaurant and this man working behind the counter are terrible also I’ve seen mice running across the lobby while waiting for my food and another time I went for chicken tenders I figure you can’t mess up deep frying chicken tenders but to my surprise he did smh not cooked all the way this guy is terrible and small portions expensive I don’t not recommend this place at all matter fact I recommend anyone that’s hungry and o not visit this restaurant ever in your life!!!!

Second time here and both visits were great.  Pizza is tasty.  The end crust is very crunchy and flavorful.  The 16 inch for $3 more gave us an extra meal.  It wouldn't even fit in the 12 inch box.  Plenty of seating for dine in.

We recently took a trip from Philadelphia down to Baltimore, Maryland to visit a little place we've been wanting to check out - Dodah's Kitchen. Known for their fantastic vegan cakes in Philadelphia, it was a no-brainer to stop by. They are 100% vegan and we've heard so many good things about their food, we had to try it for ourselves.

Arriving on a Friday around 5 PM, the place wasn't too busy as people were likely on their way home from work. The ambiance had a nice vibe, despite the cold air conditioning blasting at 60°. It took a little bit of searching to find someone at the counter, and there was a small language barrier as the person mostly spoke Spanish. However, pointing at certain items helped clear the confusion. After requesting to turn off the air conditioning, things started to feel more comfortable.

The layout of the restaurant was unique, with plants covering each table for added privacy. With nice background music playing, we finally decided on our order - vegan barbecued ribs, breaded vegan fried chicken wings, seafood mac & cheese, regular mac & cheese, breaded vegan fried shrimp, and a shrimp wrap. It was a lot of food, but we wanted to try a bit of everything.

The food arrived in about 15 minutes, and we asked for takeout containers in anticipation of the large portions. The breaded vegan fried chicken wings were a pleasant surprise, tasting so close to real chicken. The vegan ribs were delicious with just the right amount of barbecue sauce. The seafood mac & cheese had a nice flavor, though we weren't sure about the seafood chunks.

Overall, our experience was good. Though I'm not a big fan of comfort food, Dodah's Kitchen has won me over with their vegan options. I particularly enjoyed the vegan chicken wings and ribs. And their cakes are a must-try if you have the chance. They truly stand out in the vegan dessert department.

Ordered to go and loved the portions. I've had their Mac n cheese from MOM's Organics so I was excited to see they had a location in DC and wanted to try more food. The general tso cauliflower is very good! I love their vegan cheesecake as well!

I visited Duda’s today around 2-ish with my son, who is a vegetarian. We were both really looking forward to enjoying a meal together. I’ve been to Duda’s before—years ago—and I remembered having an amazing chicken sandwich and a warm, welcoming vibe, so I was excited to return.

I ordered the sweet kale, garlic kale, chickpea salad, and the cauliflower tofu with rice. Unfortunately, the experience didn’t match my expectations this time.
•	The kale dishes, although flavorful, tasted like they hadn’t been washed properly. There was a sandy texture in both, and I had to stop eating them.
•	The cauliflower tofu bites were mostly dough rather than cauliflower, even though the sauce itself was good.
•	The rice wasn’t warm, which made the dish less enjoyable overall.

The chickpea salad was great.

On top of the food, the atmosphere felt very different from my first visit. We weren’t greeted when we walked in, even though people were already seated and eating. The table available had food left on it, so we couldn’t sit and eat right away. Overall, it just didn’t feel as warm or welcoming as before, which was disappointing because I genuinely wanted this to be a good experience—especially for my son.

I’m not expecting anything in return; I just wanted to offer honest feedback about my visit today. I’ve had great experiences here in the past, so I hope this helps improve things moving forward.

As a vegetarian I obviously I'm excited that a restaurant such as this exists. But I have to be honest I was a bit disappointed by the food. The portion sizes are large which I appreciated. But the taste was very starchy and carb heavy.  The homemade sauce of that orange chicken or whatever it is was not great either. A lot of the side dishes were not fresh and clearly have been sitting there for a while. To be fair we went right before they closed.  They had to make a new batch of ribs which took about half hour. The guy working there was very nice.  I really hate knocking this place, because I wish there were more vegan restaurants. But I don't think I'll return. Prices there are quite high, too.

Paid $37 for a truly disappointing meal. I originally ordered the drummies but was told they were sold out only after placing the order. I was then offered tenders and crab cakes as substitutes. For sides, I chose mac and cheese and quinoa.

After a 25-minute wait, I opened the box to find food that looked unappetizing — and unfortunately, it tasted even worse. The tenders were mediocre, the crab cakes were bland, and the mac and cheese was barely edible. I ended up throwing away 80% of the meal.

The only redeeming part of the experience was the Colada Moss drink — that was excellent. Everything else was a waste of money. I miss Grub Factory — the food was better, and the chef actually knew what they were doing.

name: Caribbean Dynasty Restaurant & Lounge
vicinity: 647 W Pratt St Suite B, Baltimore

reviews.text: We came in from out of town and stumbled upon this place after leaving another local bar. When we sat at the bar the bartender greeted us gave us a menu and mentioned the specials. She was very nice loved her vibe. I had i believe a blueberry wine which was delicious and the honey lemon pepper wings which were also delicious 10/10 i wish i order more to go . There’s a separate dinning area and the bathrooms were clean and tidy. Would def come back !

The food was decent. I never had cabbage with mixed vegetables in it. My curry chicken was good with the exception of 2 pieces of chicken that was not tender. The service was not very friendly which makes me not want to spend my money. Also there's No Pepper Sauce. It was an experience but no where I'd come back to.
Came here on a Friday night and had the goat roti (amazing) and fried plantains (these should be classified as a drug). Awesome people, music, and food. It’s not a restaurant, it’s a vibe

The jerk chicken was tasty, but the portion size was pretty small once you factor in the bones (the pieces were very boney).

The prices were a bit high for the portion size. And they automatically add 20% tip to ask orders, which is annoying. They were also out of a bunch of stuff from the menu.

The decor was very much a "makeup on a pig" situation, but it was functional. But they had a TV behind the bar showing news with the volume way too loud.

The server was friendly and explained some of the menu items to us. The food came out pretty quick.

Great service and delicious food. I was craving oxtail for Christmas dinner and I was able to pick up my order on Christmas eve. Sheldon and the other staff were friendly and welcoming and the oxtail was delicious.

Johnny’s was an absolutely delightful experience from start to finish. The moment I walked in, I was impressed by the warm atmosphere, the inviting setup, and the sheer abundance of food options. This place easily ranks in my top three best brunch spots I’ve EVER visited.

Every dish was cooked to absolute perfection — the flavors, the presentation, everything was spot on. I still catch myself thinking about how good that meal was to this day. The service only made the experience better; the staff was attentive, friendly, and made sure everything was just right.

If you’re looking for a brunch that truly stands out and leaves a lasting impression, Johnny’s is the place. I’ll definitely be returning!

This place is absolutely wonderful. I particularly love that they change their menus often and always have options for all dietary restrictions and they are tucked away in a tree-lined street. Helen and all of the staff is always kind and knowledgeable on menu preferences. If I could add one thing to Johnny's, that would be for them to bring the flowers and farmer's market back. It was a huge hit and highlight for patrons in the past and I truly miss it.
Lovely outdoor seating - service was awesome. Food was 50/50 … corn soup was great. Veggies on the hummus tray weren’t on par

Johnny's is a quiet and cozy spot nestled in a historic north Baltimore location.

The staff was friendly and accommodating. They were decorating for the Christmas holiday, which added to the warm atmosphere. You can have a seat at one of two bars or grab a table.

The food was delicious! We ordered fried oysters and muscles to start. All cooked to perfection. I ordered an Angus burger medium rare with a fried egg and Johnny's in-house cole slaw on the side. The slaw was fresh and crispy. It was flavorful with just the right amount of sauce.  The burger got a bit sloppy towards the end, but most really good burgers do. My wife had the salmon, which she really enjoyed.
The prices were reasonable as well.

All in all, our time and money was well spent, and  we'll be back in the future.

This was my first experience. I went with my sister and two friends. The atmosphere was lovely, but it was so dimly lit in there. You can barely see the menus. I think they were going for intimate type vibe but just a little bit more light would’ve been nice. What yall hiding in there 👀? Just kidding. Anyways, our servers were awesome though and we even had other servers check in on us and give us recommendations.
We went for restaurant week. I put a picture below of the deal. The cocktail of the mouth was really good. It was a captain Morgan based drink. The calamari was disappointing. It was called crispy calamari, but was not crispy at all. The short rib was good and so was the blueberry cheesecake. I have to say I was a little disappointed with the proportions. I get that it is restaurant week, but it felt like the proportions were kid sized. Overall, we did enjoy ourselves and I would go back again to try the food outside of restaurant week.

9/17/2025
My first afghan restaurant and on a nice rainy day. I ended up here with help of the timeleft app, was seated as soon as I walked in the door. I started with the AUSHAK and a glass of white wine. Both were great I love how tender the pasta is, the yogurt mixed with the cilantro sauce( they give for the table) by far is the best combo. The naan was thick and such a good touch to soak up all the pasta sauce. Ended up the meal with the afghan style  ice cream which had a taste that I was not used to. I loved the fresh fruits and the cardamom in the ice cream had my tastebuds singing. The seating has 2 areas and a nice little bar in the back.  I noticed a new customers coming in and requesting single seating which was not a problem for this spot. Our server was very punctual clearing plates, getting refills I just would have loved to hear about the new items and drinks that were on the table before I ordered.
Bathroom rating:5/5

Delicious and unique. Stopped by for a solo dinner, very friendly and professional staff, large space, good wine and cocktail selection and so many food options! Haven't had Afghani food before and this was a treat. Ordered the salmon specialty and some bread. Highly recommend and would come back on a future trip.

⭐️⭐️⭐️ 3.3/5 stars

We visited The Helmand on a Thursday night and were surprised to find it almost completely empty. Just two other diners were in the entire restaurant, which gave it a strange, somewhat lifeless vibe for a place that gets so much hype online.

The decor feels a bit outdated, and honestly, they could probably use some marketing help to get more people through the door. It really didn’t feel like a spot that’s supposed to be one of Baltimore’s most famous Afghan restaurants.

That said, the service was excellent. The servers were super attentive, always checking on us and refilling our water without us having to ask. They were polite and knowledgeable about the menu.

The food itself was… fine. A lot of the menu revolves around lamb, which was cooked well enough but didn’t blow us away. Flavors were decent, but nothing stood out as particularly memorable. It’s the sort of meal where you finish full and satisfied but not raving about it afterward.

We didn’t try any of the wine or coffee, so can’t comment on those, but the prices were fair for the amount of food we got.

Overall, it was a solid experience, but I’m just not sure it deserves the level of hype it gets online. Tasty, but not amazing. If you’re curious about Afghan food or just want something different, it’s worth trying at least once, but don’t go in expecting to be completely wowed.

I was first a little skeptical of visiting because I had previously DoorDash'd food from The Helmand and wasn't super enthused. However, they really delivered when it comes to in-house meals. I visited with a party of over 10 and they were able to accomodate us and serve us quickly. They have lots of fantastic vegetarian options revolving around rice, lentils, and curries. Everything we had was colorful and flavorful. Would definitely love to visit again.

This restaurant has gone downhill since the original owner died, which is a shame because this place was such a historic and iconic staple for the DMV Afghan diaspora. I’ve been to this restaurant in the past and always had an incredible experience. Now, the food is not authentic, the portions for some dishes are ridiculously small, and the atmosphere feels cheapened (they had paper tablecloths on the tables).

The mantu appetizer only came with just a single piece of mantu. I’ve never seen that before in any Afghan restaurant I’ve been to. Most restaurants give at least 3-4 pieces. Also, the mantu was served on a plate of dal (lentils). That’s not how authentic mantu is made in Afghan culture at all.

The chicken was very good, but the rice and dips really tasted like a terrible mockery/knock off of South Asian cuisine rather than authentic Afghan cuisine, which is supposed to taste more like a blend of West and Central Asian food usually.

The firnee did not taste authentic at all. The pudding had no flavor and it was missing crushed pistachios—which is one of the most key ingredients for firnee. However, the falooda ice cream did taste good.

Overall, this place isn’t terrible, but it’s not authentic, and you’d be much better off by going to DC or northern Virginia for Afghan food instead. This place just isn’t it anymore.

Hidden gem near the city center. Flavorful food of high quality which is beautifully presented. Puerto 511 only offers a prix fixe menu of either 5 or 6 dishes (depending on the day). Plan for a 2 hour dining experience as service is on the slower side but the food is well worth the wait!

Incredible, unassuming Peruvian restaurant in Baltimore! We did the weeknight tasting menu and loved all 5 courses, particularly the ceviche and anticucho. Highly recommend bringing your own pisco like we did as they’ll make you pisco sours. Will definitely be back!
Amazing restaurant hands down the best $60 meal I have ever had! You will have to ring the buzzer to get in. Every part of the 5 course tasting menu was delicious!

Excellent and authentic Peruvian food - you'll leave with revelations about potatoes.  I've been trying to recreate his leche de tigre at home for years. Still haven't succeeded.

It's an ever shifting pre-fix menu, so you'll always have the thrill of novelty combined with the certainty of success.

The interior is, unfortunately, painted millennial gray, but it's got lots of cheerful art and they've fixed the lighting, so it's still pretty pleasant to sit it. They don't refresh your cutlery between courses.

Chef Jose Victorio Alarcon is immensely talented and very personable. He trains people well, so even when he's not in the kitchen, you'll get food at his quality. He also operates the much more casual EMPA511 in  Fells Point, which is an great place for a very efficient and delicious lunch.

A very cute place with sincere food and I greatly enjoyed my visit :) It's hidden in the corner street and you'll have to find the white door and ring to get in. Great tasting menu with a reasonable price. Every dish was well thought-out and full of details. The dishes were generally on the sour side, which I greatly enjoy, but if you don't like sourness it might be too much. We also ordered chicha morada and I really liked it. The service was attentive while not disruptive. I also liked the interior decorations!

So far, so great!!
I am late to the Streets Market and Cafe party, but I am present.

I overheard colleagues discussing this place and had immediate FOMO!!
I visited for the 1st time 2 weeks ago, and I have been at least 4-5 times already.

I love how fresh the food is on the hot deli bar, and I am so thankful that it's behind protective glass for an employee to gather and present instead of it being in an open area, etc.

Although the cashiers are normally less than excited to see any customer, they work fast, and efficient. It works for me.

I will surely continue to support this market and recommend to friends and family.

This is a great little supermarket.   Yes, prices are high. But that is how it is in the heart of the city.  They have a large and diverse selection of products.....Meat  dairy, produce, wine, kitchen basics, cheese, fresh fish.   If you live in the city, you know how fortunate it is to have an actual grocery story that isn't just a glorified bodega.  They have quality products.  Look for what's on sale. I got locally grown apples for .59 a pound.

I'm here multiple times per week and God do I hate it! The reason I'm there so often is that it's the only grocery that's nearby on foot that has more or less the full range of items I'd typically need. I find everything here to be obscenely expensive, though, for reference, not very different from Whole Foods. The reason I find it so unpleasant, is that now that I've taken the time to figure out which are the items that are still affordable and cannot be acquired as easily elsewhere, it's still the case that they're constantly out of stock on items, and once they are, it will often be for weeks at a time (or even indefinitely). Additionally, many items don't have a price or have the wrong price (which never gets corrected). So, in addition to being expensive, it is also unreliable.

That said, the cashiers at the register are all extremely efficient, and even when there's a line, it goes quickly.

People are nice, check out is quick, but don't have variety of employees all one race, prices are higher than other grocery stores, see large variety of ready to go food, produce is not as fresh especially packaged ones they go bad next day or two, and some are already no good, otherwise they have a lot of things to choose from. They need to have more sales or discounts, extremely overpriced. They don't sell separate items so if u need 2 peppers for ur meal u have to spend more and buy a whole pack. The meat and fish look good. But sometimes it smells in there. Could just be the fish. Not sure though. Overall it's a good quick spot to get what u need in a hurry to make quick meal, just not good for full fridge grocery shopping. Too pricey for that. *I recently saw 2  people of different race, working in the evening. So that's good representation of the local neighborhood. Good job Streets!

Idk why this place has high reviews. Maybe I have high standards, who knows. No greeting, don't really respond to anything you say, extremely unfriendly, on shift supervisor/manager refused to see me, the floor employee was really hesitant in giving me his name and the GMs contact or business card, also according to some of the staff and security the general managers doesnt really care for customer service complaints. I just moved to the neighborhood and I was pretty excited about this place cuz it was close by but I'm just never going back there again. Just my 2cents in case you're new to the neighborhood or have never been and wanted to try it out. The prices aren't all that great either, I'm all about local businesses but local business gotta try a little too.
Super cute coffee shop! Partner and I went here every morning during our stay in Baltimore. Highly recommend the bagel breakfast sandwich

We visited this place twice during our trip to Baltimore and became my favorite spot during our stay. The food was great. The service was solid although we did have a bad experience the second time. The atmosphere is very bright and roomy.

The iced lavender matcha latte was amazing. The flavors were balanced and flavorful. The lox cream cheese bagel was also great. Tons of fresh ingredients and flavorful.

The service was great during our first visit. During our second visit, we were waiting forever for our food. We brought it to their attention, showed them the receipt and they were confused as if they never got the order. They immediately got to getting the food done but this experience lost them a star despite how much I like the place.

The atmosphere is great. Definitely a place where you can just hangout or do work on your laptop
This spot is in a fantastic location!  It seems perfect for telework and the staff is friendly and in great spirits. My latte was delicious and the design was great even though I had oat milk.
Great coffee spot near Baltimore inner harbor. Nice place to warm up before/after strolling around the city. Excellent milk preparation, I’ve never seen a silkiest latte. 11/10.

Just bought my first coffee beans that weren’t covered in chocolate here! I recently got my hands on a French Press & have been doing tons of online research with the hopes of putting things together in real time. Garrett (hope I spelled that right) is so knowledgeable he walked me through the beans & my flavor profile & what I hope to accomplish (which is to stop spending $5+ a day on Americanos that I believe will be more rewarding to brew at home.) I am so glad I wandered in & I can’t wait to take that first sip at home!

The Neighborhood Bird Bowl was fantastic and way more than I could eat in a single meal. I got the spicy variant and was not disappointed. The pickled vegetables on the side go very well with the Taiwanese curry fried chicken.

As I believe has been mentioned in other reviews, there is not a lot of seating space. Just a few bar stools. I was lucky and happened to hit it right in-between busy periods, so I didn't have a problem finding a sera but something to be aware of.

My wife and I went to Ekiben after being at a nearby brewery. This was our first time to one of their locations and it did not disappoint at all. We both got the spicy neighborhood bird bun and it was the greatest spicy chicken sandwich we have ever had. The chicken was flavorful and and crispy, the bun was soft and pillowy, and the sauce had the perfect amount of heat without drowning out the flavor of the sauce.
I would recommend this place every single time and we will be going back very soon.

The food was delicious! 😍 The best Brokkoli I have ever eaten!
I heard it once and always remembered
Ekiban is the food of Baltimore 🙌🏽
The food was truly a treat, even though we had to wait for 20 min, the music was great and I cannot wait to eat there again ✨

This place was over-hyped all over TikTok and Instagram, so I had high expectations—but it was disappointing. The chicken was raw, and when I pointed it out to the server, he simply over-fried it instead of properly remaking it, which ruined the texture and taste.

On the positive side, the vegetables and rice were fresh, and the sides were decent. However, that doesn’t make up for poor food handling and service.

Would I go back? No. The hype doesn’t match the quality, and raw chicken is a deal-breaker.

Health: While fried food doesn’t lend itself to the most healthy diet, the blend of white rice, kimchi, and legitimate Asian/American fusion veggies tossed in soy sauce and not grilled in oil balances it out.

Price: For this taste and portion size? Excellent. Though not particularly “low”. Definitely satisfying though.

Experience: The most “alive” and “trendy” food scene in Baltimore. Small restaurant, big heart. I got my second meal there for free due to being a government medical researcher during furlough. But regardless, clean, convenient, and speedy. Great on all accounts.

Taste: A genuinely unique Asian/American fusion. Where other locations will rehash food drowned in oil, this place takes the best American and East Asian food elements and balances them excellently. Asian sauces over fried chicken. White rice with kimchi. Large protein and veggie portions with rice accompaniment (that’s the actual way real Asian food is served by the way). Honestly unique and Amazing.

Yeah I’m coming back here again. And I already have. So is everyone else in town. A core port of Baltimore’s food scene. A cornerstone of Asian/American fusion in general. Food and culture wise.

Agree with others, lamb haneeth is a must order. Didn’t get as many piece of lamb as other pictures shown here. It was delicious - cooked perfectly tender with so much flavor. I don’t know what kind of magic is going with the orange colored rice, but they were so scrumptious. Heard a regular order more orange rice - the plate came out with mostly orange rice instead of a mix of orange and white. The hummus was perfectly seasoned and light as a cloud. The SOUP was good.

Some of the best yemini food we ever had. We got Appetizer sampler, Meat hummus, Chicken Mandi, Lamb haneeth, Lamb salta. The flavor was amazing and the meat is very tender. Definitely check this place out.

Don’t forget to get their tea!

Walking into this hole-in-the-wall eatery is like a warm hug. You are engulfed not only by the anticipated flavors of the food, but a tangible vibration that tinges of love. The aromas begin wafting your senses as you approach the entrance. We are partial to the lamb options, however the menu also includes fish and chicken. You have the choice to pair your protein with their signature orange rice with beans, or fresh baked clay oven bread. Non-meat options include falafel, grape leaves, baba ganouch, selection of salads and the creamiest hummus I have ever encountered. Soup is made fresh to accompany whichever entrée you choose. Hot sweet tea with milk or without sits reliably on the table for your self-serve. There is a busy first floor eating area for convenience, however, a 2nd floor space provides a calm quiet experience for those who are willing to climb. For the quick takeout at midnight, the lamb wrap is a filling go-to for under $10. Don’t be the one to miss out on this Baltimore diamond-in-the-rough.

One of my favorite places in Fells Point!! I highly recommend the hummus and the lamb haneeth which literally falls off the bone. Or if you want a quick snack, the lamb wrap never fails. They certainly have the best lamb in the city. Go check it out!

Amazing authentic middle eastern food! Serving sizes are plentiful and each dish is made to perfection. My boyfriend and I got hummus, yoghurt, rice, fries, and 2 chicken sandwiches. The chicken sandwich is so big we split one, and will have leftovers for a while after this. Delicious food and we will be returning!

Update: Years later and this restaurant is still a staple to my friends and I! We visited during Ramadan and the in-person dining experience couldn’t have been better. Truly authentic, delicious Arabic cuisine. The employees are so kind and personable. They make it an amazing experience each time whether we dine in or take it to go. This is the ONLY place I get Arabic food from!

I came here with my family after visiting the aquarium. We are out-of-towners. From the food to the spectacular service from Ms. Candy we will most definitely be back. The food is authentic and everything is cooked in house. I’m not sure what I liked more, the AMAZING fresh sweet potato pie with the graham cracker crust or the perfectly crispy chicken wings, the jerk wings were amazing and the salmon was banging. The sides were 10/10. Mac and cheese, collard greens and cabbage. Even the French fries were perfect lol And again, Ms. Candy was a pleasant waitress and hostess, she was for sure the queen of the spot! Google only allows photos and I took videos of the meals, but pls enjoy the photo of the French fries haha

I ordered through a delivery service. The food arrived and was absolutely awful. I was not even able to eat it. The quality was terrible. The greens string beans were 2 different colors ( old mix with newer) the fried chicken was clearly sourced cheep and of poor quality.

Me and my bf ordered from uber eats, i asked for cabbage got greens instead, no biggie, i usually pick at my chicken bc i dont like eating veins or chicken that has blood on it but this day i was literally starving so i js ate it without looking but the next piece i tore apart bc i wanted to dip it in ranch, i saw a bunch of pink immediately thrown off. I thought it was js tht one piece but no all of them were like tht. My bf ate like 3 pieces before i told him we cant eat this we’re gonna get salmonella. Sure enough the entire day i had the runs, my stomach hurted nonstop even when i didn’t have to use the bathroom. Thankfully i got my money back from uber eats but this is very unsafe i strongly advise the kitchen to do better.
The greens were a 6/10 needs better seasonings and the mac was a 7/10 not too bad.

I ordered via UberEats. I got the catfish platter with mac&cheese and greens and sweet potato pie. The catfish was DELICIOUS. The homemade tartar sauce was so nice and unique. The mac and cheese was interesting but the more I ate it the more I liked it. The greens were gross to me. I threw them away. Sweet potato pie had different flavors than I am used to but I also liked it. Overall I will order again but SKIP THE GREENS!

This food was okay ..not gonna lie my stomach became very upset after eating tho. The atmosphere was not what I expected, very dull and need some lighting. Looks like they don't get business much. I had crab cake greens & yellow rice. My rice was hard , crab cake was a 2/10 and the greens were phony! never again for me. lady at the front desk was very sweet tho

Blacksauce Kitchen is well known around the city for dishing up those big buttery biscuit sandwiches we've all seen at the farmers market.  I finally had the opportunity to try their brick and mortar location in Remington for a delicious early afternoon bite.

Blacksauce is a quaint little shop with limited seating options to enjoy your food.  I decided to grab my food to go and pop a squat down the street at R. House to eat my lunch. The staff at Blacksauce were welcoming and very friendly. I decided to go with the Cider Braised Chicken Biscuit, Sweet Potato Donut, and a Smoked Apple Cider.  The chicken biscuit was yummy, especially with the addition of the onion jam which seemed to appear more prominent and even more flavorful once the sandwich was cold.  I enjoyed the sweet potato donut however, I wanted more of a sweet potato flavor to shine through.  And the smoked apple cider drink was just what was needed for the cooler weather.

I follow Blacksauce Kitchen on IG and they always seem to have some really creative dishes they make on a weekly basis.  I definitely plan on stopping by to try more of their lunch/dinner style food on a Thursday.

Let's get into it!!!!! Ooooo weeeee!!! Blacksauce Kitchen is the truth. The menu changes daily so let's get into Thursdays (Aug 17th) menu choices. We ordered 1 of everything left on the menu: Oxtail biscuit, doubles, mac, cabbage, cobbler, fritters, sorrel and limeade. We stayed inside the restaurant to make sure we tasted everything fresh and hot. They have one table and a bar top with stools for dining in.

10/10 my favorite was the cabbage. Perfect seasoning, heat, cook - no complaints whatsoever. I could eat a pot full.

9/10 my second favorite was the oxtail biscuit. The picture below speaks for itself. Ghr biscuit was PERFECTION!! I could've used some kind of sauce or wetness on the oxtail. The fried onions were on point.

8.5/10 the fritters were great. The each chow chow gave it that extra edge. Because it was served in a recyclable container all the chose chow juices were absorbed in the container. J think it should be served in plastic. Or foil placed in the container.

7/10 the Mac was good. 8/10 Sorrel was great. We actually created a half and half of sorrel and limeade and that was fire 10/10. The doubles were good but could've been cooked longer. The only thing we weren't fans of was the smoked cobbler. Wag too much smoke for my taste. The smokey flavor overwhelmed the cobbler.

Most definitely going back to hit another menu soon!!
Rotating menu and well known biscuits food never disappoints truly unique experience.

I did an online order for a rotisserie chicken apricot biscuit and it was delicious! My order was ready right on time for the time that I scheduled to pick it up. It was also a nice portion size, which I loved. The peach jam on the biscuit really made all the flavors standout!

Had their yuzu plum donut when they were at the Ekiben Night Market today. It was one of the best donuts I’ve ever had. Not too sweet, great citrus flavor, and the crunchiness of the donut on the outside was amazing. I hope you guys make it a regular part of your menu because it was the bomb.

Amazing late night dinner. And delicious cocktails. The lighting is nice and low and good music too. Had the blackened catfish and mac and cheese (pictured after we already started eating). Whole heartedly recommend!

Service was great. Our waiter was very attentive. Food came out hot and everything was a 10/10 for taste and portions. We got the honey old bay wings, hen, mash potatoes, spinach, catfish, mac and cheese and collard greens! Happy hour prices were great. All that food plus 6 drinks ( tip included) was less than $200.
Happy Hour was cute. Drinks are good. Crab dip was too cream cheesy. But the shrimp was Poppin. Would definitely visit again. Vibes was great. Waiter was top notch

The oxtail and grits were so good! Nice hole in the wall neighborhood spot and plays really good music without it being too loud or overpowering! Had a brunch here with 4 ladies and it was the perfect ambiance

I been here three times this week this place is so fire. Food is amazing and cocktails amazing. These the only photos I have but definitely not the best menu items, I think they got the best crab cakes and sauce in bmore

I drove to the new location at 1029 W Baltimore St and there is not a restaurant with this name over here. I called the number, it played an automated message with the location changed and new opening date. Today is January 8th. I called to see if there is a person that can direct us to the correct place, but couldn't reach a person. Per Google, they should be open.

Amazing food and service!
We walked in without a reservation, and we were seated promptly and were introduced to the menu. Their signature peach ice tea was so delicious and sweet! The complimentary corn bread with sweet potato butter was to die for. We also had the crab Mac & cheese, the baby back ribs, and the fried catfish and grits. All were so delicious. The catfish and grits especially were really good. The service was great and our drinks were kept full.
One of the best meals in Baltimore for sure!

Black owned, family run restaurant. Food and drinks were delicious. The chicken was slightly undercooked and they didn't hesitate to put the skillet back in the oven. It came back fully cooked and delicious!

I'd recommend: Cornbread skillet (perfect for sharing), BBQ chicken w mac & cheese and collard greens, and BBQ ribs w mash and asparagus.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Darker than Blue in Baltimore, and I must say, the experience was absolutely amazing. From the moment I walked in, I was impressed by the warm and friendly customer service. The staff went above and beyond to make sure our group of 12 felt welcome and comfortable.

Now, let's talk about the food. Oh my goodness, it was simply outstanding! Every dish we tried was bursting with flavor and expertly prepared. Whether you're a seafood lover or prefer something more savory, Darker than Blue has something to satisfy every palate. The menu offers a wide variety of options, and each dish is crafted with care and attention to detail.

In addition to the incredible food, I was also blown away by the quality of the drinks. The bartenders at Darker than Blue truly know their craft and create delicious and refreshing beverages. I highly recommend trying one of their signature cocktails or exploring their extensive wine list.

Overall, my experience at Darker than Blue was nothing short of exceptional. The combination of delectable food, top-notch customer service, and inviting atmosphere make it a must-visit restaurant in Baltimore. I would rate my experience a perfect 10/10 and will definitely be returning in the future.

My experience here was perhaps one of my worst dining experiences In Baltimore. The bartender/waiter was not friendly at all. He gave off the energy that we were some how inconveniencing him by being there from the moment we walked in the door. They don't have a drink menu, had no beer at all, no burgers (we found out after ordering), and  the dishes were dirty. When we brought to bartender that our wine glasses were dirty, he said its from the dish washer and there was nothing  he could do about that but pour it in to another glass. As if we had to take it or leave it. Which my wife and are choosing to leave it and never consider going there again. We thought maybe the food would end up being good in the end despite the poor service but they missed the mark on that as well. We ordered the lemon pepper wings and they had little to no flavor. We were really excited to try this place since we are locals but unless there is a dramatic change in the attitude of the staff and improvement in the quality of service overall, they wont make it unfortunately.
Great music cute atmosphere. brunch was really good. The potatoes were so good. Tubs served us a multitude of mimosa flavors the guava was the best! I will definitely be back

I went to First Fridays at Empanada Lady and had an amazing time. The vibe was great! There was music playing, people dancing, and the food…as always was DELICIOUS!!! They have the best empanadas in Baltimore! Make sure you check them out!

Very cozy spot near Inner Harbor. Had a fantastic meal here - excellent empanadas and sides. Service was excellent despite being busy; the bartender was very friendly, accommodating, and patient with us while we ordered. The cocktails were great. The platter for one person is HUGE, definitely hits the spot if you are super hungry. Standout sides were the tostones and street corn. The salmon, chicken, and beef empanadas are fantastic. The apple empanada was delicious as a “dessert” empanada.

Took my Mom out for a late lunch yesterday 12-18-2025 around 3:00pm. We arrived in the restaurant and there's only one man at the bar the restaurant was empty and quiet , we were told to sit anywhere near the window due to them setting up for a party... okay cool.. Mom and I sit down scan the menu, the waiter came took our drink orders, explained the menu since we were new customers. Since we came with an appetite we were ready and very excited to try the empanadas.

We ordered the combo platter that comes with 6 different empanadas a choice of 2 sides and 2 cupcakes for dessert..for  $60.99 I got a Modelo Mom got a Coke.. Somehow the bill ended up being $90+

Anyway the waiter brought our chips and salsa out first then the nadas and our second side of plantains. The chips and salsa were fair.. we were expecting more of a tortilla style of chip though and the salsa had a marinara sauce taste. The empanadas were delicious but could have been fried slightly less they were fried very hard.

My problem was mainly about how we were treated our server never came back to ask how the food was ask if we needed refills or anything. When he finally came back he said he was preoccupied with setting up that event, so he knew he wasn't attentive to us, when I asked for the boxes and check the seemed to struggle with proving everything all at once which left me so get up go to the bar to get the physical check, that's when I realized we didn't get the cupcakes we were looking forward to.. waiter said he gave us two slices of cake for the troubles but I told him we didn't want the cake we preferred the cupcakes to which he said the cake was better but it wasn't it was coconut (we both don't like that flavor)   Waiter asked if we would be returning I told him likely it due to lack of interest the restaurant seemed to have in us dining in.

***I will come back to update this post later to recheck my receipt because I'm not understanding that price of the final bill..

What a great gem in the heart of the city. Thoroughly enjoyed my food, atmosphere, and service. Taylor was a great bartender.   She was friendly and had a great knowledge of the drinks. The food was filling and delicious. I visited on a Thursday night and parking was pretty easy. This is definitely a great place with a chill vibe. I highly recommend the salmon, pork and chicken empanadas.  Also a great place to purchase art from local artists.

All I wanted was a simple egg and cheese with butter. That's all. Nothing special. But when I began to eat it! I just knew somebody in that kitchen made my sandwich with love. Thank you. You made my day. I hope you have a reason to smile every day. Just because of that sandwich.
Their customer service is top-notch, making you feel valued every time.

There only reason why I gave them one star is because of the fries but if I wanted a kids meal I’ll go to McDonald’s next time.
3 wings and fries $8.00….this is a freaking kids meal
I remember4 wings and fries were $6.00
There prices now is crazy to be a carry Out
The wings are smaller and the boxes got even smaller
Don’t waste your money, next time I’ll go to Hip Hop across the street.
Best Lake trout in east Baltimore 👌. Big pieces.

The steak egg and cheese breakfast sandwich is SO good. My wife and I get that sandwich every morning. And it is so worth the 6 dollars. Best 6 dollars I've ever spent, honestly. I'll wait for it to open instead of goin elsewhere. We're very loyal customers. And they are so friendly. Great prices on everything. But breakfast food is the best, at least I think.

Around 2:30pm on a Wednesday I walked into this place due to the Jamaican place across the street not having what I wanted to order. I was about to get in my car and saw this soul food cafe and figured I'd give it a try and I also needed to feed me and my hungry toddler after running errands.
Walking into the establishment it looked dirty and in need of TLC. Mind you for this side of town I wasn't expecting too much. I was in line behind 1 person, l had already overheard the cashier/cook telling the customer he didn't have the item he wanted so the customer ordered something else, it was a meat option. The guy goes to the back of the store and I'm still standing there. I pickup 1 of the 2 menus on the counter to look it over & immediately noticed how sticky the menus were.
In come two females that I wouldn't have assumed worked there, I noticed they had supplies in their hand and walked to the back of the cafe behind the counter. I hear a small argument and cursing ensue and then 1 of the girls comes to the front to take my order. I'm vegetarian so l usually order sides platters from soul places. I asked the girl if any of the veggies contained meats to which she stated 1 of them did not so I asked her for the cabbage, yams and macaroni, she told me to hold on and then walked to the back to ask if they had those items. I overhear the other lady (manager) that walked in tell her we don't have ANY sides except macaroni. The girl comes back to relay the message and I tell her that's fine I'll just get the macaroni so I could at least put something on my toddlers stomach and I pay for the macaroni. The girl walks to the back to get the macaroni and I overhear the manager again state it's not going to be ready for another 10 mins. She comes back out again to let me know this and at this point I just wait thinking that "well at least it will be fresh" then the cashier takes more orders. She walks to the back and grabs my food and starts bagging it.
I suddenly realized from the time she walked into the store to handing me my food and handling my utensils that she did not wash her hands & there were never any gloves involved. At this point I convinced myself that at least she didn't make the food and that she only handled the containers. I waited until I got home to open the bag and was disgusted with how much grease was seeping off the containers. The appearance of the Mac & cheese was questionable looking burnt, the taste was VERY questionable!
I've never tasted macaroni and cheese as bad as that it tasted sour, I've had better boxed macaroni & cheese.

I found them on social media , the way they likely the manager responds to customers on their social media is disrespectful and nasty!

The owner should take more pride in her brand. Having several item on the menu unavaliable does not show pride. Having customers wait for an hour for there order that should have been 20 minutes is not taking pride. We didn't so much as receive a "sorry for the wait" but watched as she took her friend or BF to the bar across the street. If that is the attitude towards your business it won't last long. IT COULD BE A GOLD MINE. But the owner need to get serious and have a better business initiatives.
Like down size the menu for a carryout.  You have no seating or tables keep your star item and bring on some low cost quick items. Focus on streamlining production. If you get 4 orders you are swamped.  Lastly provide better service each guest should be a priority. You can and should do better

I ride pass this place all the time and finally decided to give it a try. I got the lobster, crab and shrimp egg rolls. It was chunks of seafood throughout. The sauce for the egg rolls is so good! While waiting for my food, other customers were there raving about the other foods that they have.  Customer service was great. Definitely will be back tomorrow and I will definitely be a regular customer here! Thank you so much!

So normally I’d never leave a review, and I’m sad I have to, but this place smh the owners disposition was just like the food BAD. I will never come back to this establishment I’m actually really shocked it’s still in business, but I traveled almost an hour to this place, it was posted on instagram so why not support my small black businesses, got there about 3:45ish walked in and it was hotter inside then the outside and the air unit from outside was inside in the corner by the door, the young man that took my order was super nice even tho he didn’t really know the menu. We asked for a few items and was told they didn’t have majority of the menu yesterday, and only 3 sides. Cabbage, Mac and candied yams. I ordered 4 platters (surf n turf, stuffed salmon, double crab cake and friend whitening) my order went in at 4:01 with out rice and asked to sub for cabbage instead that total was $146.00. He said it was cool, I forgot to add a crab cake egg roll and went back in, there was a woman there I’m assuming the woman was the owner. She snatched the paper from the young man that helped me the first time and kinda went in on him super aggressive infront of customers due to his incorrect charging (some in-house training would help) I guess and by the time she finished there was another $63.00 added to my bill, she said it would be 30 minutes, and she’d come get my ti get my food, well an hour went by and I went back in and was told it was almost done, there was another customer there and they messed up her order as well and the “owner” got mad aggressive with her also, about wings and “they only have party wings” for 20 a plate smh. Anyway….im standing there hot as hell smelling burning food, I asked the cashier if that was my food burning said no, still standing there I see food leaving out, I asked for a “lemonade” they gave me a lemon drink not lemonade which was so nasty. Another hour goes by still waiting and she comes out y’all food almost ready, the food finally comes at 5:58 two hours for what’s pictured below, $200 and something later and the food I smelt burning and mind you I head her say it was burnt and to just turn it on another side was mine. As I’m looking at it she said super aggressive “what’s wrong, you can taste it”, I closed the boxes pissed for 2 hours you gave me burnt food, the crab cakes were not edible, the lamb was rough the Mac had more grease then Mac the yams were under cooked and no flavor, the stuffed salmon was the smaller piece of salmon I’ve ever seen and she had the audacity to try to stuff a strip of salmon, the fish wasn’t cooked the saving grace was the cabbage, the seafood didn’t smell fresh at all,  the crab cake egg roll which was $13 for one small roll was decent and the only edible thing we had ,we threw away $200 plus worth of inedible food. The store was super hot and the owner has a shitty attitude, if you know you’re business is going to get more patronage due to a social media post maybe revamp some things for a smoother flow, get a fan in there if the air isn’t working, train your employees and don’t burn an order that’s over $200. Carolina kitchen would never and that’s exactly where I went after I had to throw away an order I was told would take 30 min that’s turned into 2 hours and food was burnt, didn’t smell fresh and greasy. I would have offered some constructive advice but you can tell who and who can’t take it by how they carry themselves. Ohh and when you do glove changed you’re supposed to wash your hands in between each change. Never again I want my money back honestly.

I went for a second time and I called to place an order ahead of time (the time of operation) I received no answer. When I went in around noon they told me they were just opening.   I placed an order & they were missing side items on the menu like the yams & mac n cheese. . They didn't have entrees like the crabcake. It was a huge disappointment and waited for a while. I drove here for nothing. Unprofessional and inconsistent.

I ordered the oxtails,rasta pasta, beef patties & Brussels sprouts. Everything was very tasty. Oxtails could’ve been cooked more tenderly other than that the ambiance was nice. Portions were very generous. Would come back.

YARD was such a great place for dinner/date night. We heard the brussel sprouts were amazing and they did not disappoint at all. The Jerk chicken was so flavorful and it had the perfect char to it. The curry was very good as well and the portion was excellent, they did not skimp on the shrimp in the dish. Beef patty was very good the only thing in my opinion is that you don’t need the sauce.
